Our method utilizes LLMs to deeply diagnose performance bottlenecks, generates semantically controlled candidate edits, selects the best strategy through a multi-stage verification pipeline, and distills optimization experience into reusable knowledge for continual self-improvement. We evaluate our method using seven representative strategies: four from the A-share market and three from the Crypto market. Experimental results show that our method significantly improves the Sharpe ratio across all tested strategies: the average test Sharpe increases from -0.298 to 0.538, and the best-performing strategy achieves a 199% relative improvement. Ablation studies and stress tests under stricter conditions further validate the effectiveness and robustness of the framework. Overall, this work transforms quantitative strategy optimization from costly manual trial and error into an automated and verifiable iterative paradigm, offering a new path for applying large language models to financial strategy research.
papers.title: EVOQUANT: Self-Evolving Verifier-Guided Strategy Optimization for Robust Quantitative Trading

papers.abstract: Dynamic processing of mechanical signals is crucial for soft robotics and mechanosensing, yet classical viscoelastic materials lack intrinsic tunability and quantitative design rules. We show that internal bistability provides a simple but powerful mechanism to tailor response and signal attenuation in mechanical (meta)materials. In our model, bistable elements switch discretely with an intrinsic timescale between states that differ in potential energy $ε$, equilibrium length $Δl$, and spring constant $Δk$. We combine Brownian dynamics simulations with discrete Poisson switching at rate $ν$ and a nonlinear continuum (field) theory for the macroscopic strain relaxation. The model yields closed-form solutions for the linear response and the spatial penetration depth, revealing two complementary phenomena: a universal screening mechanism (akin to the electrostatic `skin effect') that strongly reduces signal penetration when the driving frequency exceeds the internal relaxation rate, and a frequency-insensitive response plateau arising from timescale separation. The attenuation strength, expressed by a screening length, is controlled primarily by the conformational length change $Δl$, while the attenuation regime and plateau position are tuneable via $ν$. A parameter study exposes a fundamental design trade-off: larger $Δl$ strengthen dissipation but also raise the elastic energy barrier for state transitions, eventually causing state-locking where damping vanishes. Optimal attenuation thus emerges from a compromise between pronounced bistability and a surmountable barrier. Owing to its analytical tractability and generic formulation, our framework yields explicit design rules applicable to systems from biopolymers to synthetic catch bonds and metamaterials, enabling the design of soft materials with frequency-selective mechanical response.
papers.title: Tunable Signal Penetration and Response Plateaus in Bistable Mechanical Media

papers.abstract: In 2017, Keith defined and studied a multi-restricted partition function $RD^{l,t}(n)$, the number of integer partitions of n into parts that are simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct if none of the parts is divisible by $l$ and parts appear fewer than $t$ times. Thereafter, in a series of papers Buragohain et al. and Nadji et al. examined combinatorial and arithmetic properties of $RD^{l,t}(n)$. In this article, we focus on simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions in 3-colors, $RD^{l,t}_3(n)$ and establish infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 for specific values of $(l,t)$. For instance, for positive integers $n$ and $k$, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_3^{3,3}\left(3^kn+\frac{3^k+1}{2}\right)q^n\equiv0 \pmod{3^{k+1}}. \end{align*} Our approach involves Hirschhorn's H operator technique.
papers.title: On Congruences modulo powers of 3 for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partitions in $k$-Colors

papers.abstract: Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model and the interacting disordered $XXZ$ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.
papers.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression

papers.abstract: Within Einstein power-Yang-Mills gravity (EPYM), we build a rotating black hole via the Newman-Janis procedure applied to the spherically symmetric static seed, obtaining an EPYM-inspired Kerr-like metric controlled by the spin \(a\), the magnetic Yang-Mills charge \(Q\), and the power parameter \(q\). We analyse the horizon structure and the photon region, and we compute the shadow as it appears to a remote observer for different values of these parameters. Using the published Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87\(^*\) and Sgr A\(^*\), we constrain the Yang-Mills charge and the power parameter from the angular size and the Schwarzschild deviation \(δ\) of the observed images. At the Maxwell point \(q = 1\) the spin marginalized likelihood of M87\(^*\) bounds the charge to \(Q \lesssim 0.29\,M\) at \(1σ\), while the fixed-spin band intersection at \(a = 0.7\,M\) gives the weaker \(Q \lesssim 0.52\,M\) from the M87\(^*\) angular size alone. The bound weakens as \(q \to 3/2\), where the shadow diameter becomes nearly insensitive to the charge. The shadow radius also fixes the limiting absorption cross section at high frequencies and hence the energy emission rate, which is suppressed by the charge and enhanced by the power parameter. We then compute the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar on the rotating background from the leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) conditions on the Teukolsky type radial potential, finding that the oscillation frequency rises and the damping rate falls as the charge or spin increases. The power parameter leaves an imprint on the shadow size and its charge sensitivity and in the quasinormal spectrum the shift is in principle present but lies below the resolution of current detectors.
papers.title: Probing Rotating Einstein-Power-Yang-Mills Black Holes through Shadows and Quasinormal Modes: Prospects for Event Horizon Telescope Constraints

papers.abstract: High refractive index dielectrics are central to photonic applications, yet the empirical Moss rule imposes a fundamental trade-off between refractive index and optical transparency. We introduce a modified Moss rule anchored to the optical absorption edge rather than the fundamental bandgap, capturing materials where various physical mechanisms suppress absorption well above the electronic gap. Screening the Materials Project database with this metric reveals recurring chemical compositions and structural prototypes in the materials with the most promising refractive index/transparency trade-offs. These materials include chalcopyrites, Zintl pnictides, and early transition metal multi-anion chalconitrides and oxichalcogenide compounds. Hybrid density functional theory calculations reveal that the chalconitride (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 family can achieve a combination of ultra-high refractive indices, low effective masses and transparency windows extending into the UV, potentially surpassing state-of-the-art TiO2. Our results establish (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 compounds as a unique and largely unexplored material family for next-generation photonic applications.
papers.title: A modified Moss rule highlights underexplored classes of high refractive index materials

papers.abstract: In \cite{HH}, H. Huang-X.Huang introduced the generalized Reifenberg condition which describes the non-increasing property of numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls and gave a transformation theorem under this condition. In this note, we study how almost Euclidean factors of concentric geodesic balls interact with harmonic splitting maps under a lower Ricci curvature bound and prove a dimension gap for harmonic functions of almost linear growth and then derive a transformation theorem under a non-decreasing property compared with the non-increasing property above. We also construct complete manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose balls are uniformly almost $1$-Euclidean at every scale, but for which no single harmonic function can be transformed into a splitting function at all smaller scales which give a negative answer to the existence question for all-scale splitting functions in \cite{HH}.
papers.title: Transformation theorem and monotonicity of the numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls

papers.abstract: We study binary classification when the two classes are elliptical with a shared radial generator $g$. The log-likelihood ratio is then an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link $φ=\log g$. For Gaussian classes $φ$ is affine and the rule reduces to quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA); otherwise the Bayes link is not the identity. Instead of fitting this link with a spline smoother, we derive its family from the within-class law of the radius and estimate a finite fractional-power projection. We prove that the link is identifiable from the radius law, that the plug-in estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment conditions, and that the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. For $d\ge2$ and non-nested class parameters, the identity link suffices only for affine (Gaussian) generators. The bridge, GAM membership and the affine direction of this dichotomy are verified in Lean 4. We compare against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), re-implemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget. On two UCI benchmarks the derived link ties with the fitted GAM. On six financial series from three asset classes, with validation that respects temporal dependence, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM: better on CAD/USD and tied on the other five. It beats QDA on the three heaviest-tailed series (oil $[+0.023,+0.069]$, S&P 500 $[+0.039,+0.125]$, JPY/USD $[+0.009,+0.047]$) and ties elsewhere. A rate simulation with a closed-form ground truth reproduces the $\sqrt{n}$ rate and, under covariance heterogeneity, QDA's risk floor against the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The derived link thus matches a tuned GAM without smoothing-parameter selection and improves on QDA where the generator departs from the Gaussian.
papers.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis

papers.abstract: We present a theory of decaying turbulence in which the statistics of a classical flow becomes quantum mechanics in loop space. The loop functional, the average of $e^{\mathrm{i}Γ/ν}$ for the circulation $Γ$ around a loop, is the wave function, and the Navier-Stokes equation becomes the linear loop equation. An exact operator identity represents the functional as the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/ν$, with the loop parameter as time and viscosity as Planck's constant. The turbulent state is the equal-weight density matrix on a decaying trajectory, a quantum form of the ergodic hypothesis. As in quantum field theory, turbulence at infinite Reynolds number is defined by regularization and renormalization; the loop equation regularized on $N$-sided polygons has an exact manifold of decaying solutions, the Euler ensemble, labeled by rational angles and spins. As a fermionic trace, its partition function and conditional vorticity correlations become, in the local limit, Gibbs averages of two Mathieu quantum pendulums, an integrable system. The energy spectrum, given by explicit quadratures, falls as $k^{-1}\log(1/kL)$ at small $k$ and as $k^{-7/2}$ at large $k$, with $L=\sqrt{\tildeν(t+t_0)}$ and turbulent viscosity $\tildeν$. At $kL=\sqrt2$ its slope diverges as a double logarithm: the decay at fixed $k$ is singular at a finite time, and the vorticity correlation oscillates with period $\sqrt2\,πL$. The reduction to the pendulums, with the continuum and grand canonical limits at every nonzero separation, is formally verified in Lean 4 in forthcoming work by Y. Jiang, A. Migdal et al. The theory rests on stated physical hypotheses, as statistical mechanics rests on the Gibbs distribution; its comparison with simulations and experiment is so far qualitative.
papers.title: The Quantum Pendulum of Turbulent Flow: Decaying turbulence as a thermal state of an integrable system

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly issue binary verdicts - safety gates, judge decisions, value probes - and the answer is read as the model's judgment. A settled judgment should be coherent across paired phrasings of the same question: yes to "do you approve?" should mirror no to "do you oppose?". LLMs often violate this coherence, and in a yes/no question the verdict, the answer word, and the printed position coincide, so a conventional flipped-question audit yields one contrast that cannot say what moved. We introduce a crossed psychometric battery that extends the flip to full 2x2 and 2x2x2 crossings of question polarity, printed order, and answer label, separating stance from position, word, label, and verdict-role effects; an independent graded instrument estimates each model's stance $θ$ with no binary format; and a two-parameter fit (framing susceptibility $m$, decisiveness $s$) separates robustness from saturation that hides susceptibility. Applying the battery to twenty moral dilemmas - 1.35 million trials over ten frontier models from the Claude, GPT, and Gemini families in 23 reasoning configurations - we find response-form bias widespread but never uniform. The largest apparent yes-no biases are almost purely surface (word and position), while several of the newest models show the reverse: near-zero flip contrasts concealing verdict attachment up to +0.42, a component no surface counterbalance can expose, replicated across label alphabets. Requested reasoning reshapes these channels rather than removing them. When subjects state decisions in free text and a separate model transcribes them, two judge families agree on 99.3% of jointly scored transcriptions with zero opposing committed labels, and the transcribed stance converges with the graded ruler (median $r=0.87$): response form is part of the instrument, and the judgment can be measured apart from it.
papers.title: Decomposing Yes-No Bias in LLM Moral Judgment: Stance, Position, Word, and Verdict

papers.abstract: We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can form rapidly spinning black holes, our central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks enabling efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the general expectation that black holes form with small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ code, $\texttt{CMC}$, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing ``significant'' events with mass ratio $q>0.1$. After identifying optimal candidates, we explore stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with $\texttt{MESA}$ models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, with roughly $10\%$ from ``significant'' mergers. Angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of $a\simeq 0.5$ or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.
papers.title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins

papers.abstract: The LISA-Taiji dual detector network improves millihertz SGWB sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. Solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias SGWB cross correlation estimates. We use high time resolution electron density data from Wind/SWE, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the Lomb-Scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the TDI A/E channels of the LISA-Taiji network. By including finite arm propagation, Taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the SGWB parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. Although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the SGWB cross correlation estimator directly. Under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law SGWB can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty. For M2/M3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln Gμ$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. These results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. In LISA-Taiji SGWB searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.
papers.title: Effects of Solar Wind Plasma Noise on Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Searches with a Space Based Interferometer Network

papers.abstract: Across training runs of a diffusion autoencoder, we observe similar image reconstruction quality, but substantially different levels of disentanglement in the learned representations. In this work, we study how training dynamics contribute to this behaviour. By analysing training trajectories in a controlled setting - curves of reconstruction quality against disentanglement during training - we identify two recurring trajectory patterns, which we call learning regimes. These regimes differ in how reconstruction and disentanglement evolve, despite similar reconstruction at the end of training. In the reconstruction regime, models improve image fidelity before disentanglement, while in the disentanglement regime, models improve both reconstruction and disentanglement more gradually. We hypothesise that modulating shortcut pathways in the diffusion U-Net and controlling early noise-level exposure can shape trajectories. To that end, we introduce SteeringDRL, combining gated residual U-Nets with a noise curriculum to steer models towards better disentanglement. Across attribute disentanglement benchmarks, SteeringDRL has competitive disentanglement, with reduced seed sensitivity in many settings. Our method extends to spatial disentanglement with object-centric learning, improving unsupervised segmentation on synthetic and real-world datasets.
papers.title: Steering Training Trajectories in Diffusion Representation Learning

papers.abstract: Complex Java methods challenge automated unit test generation, as achieving high coverage and fault detection requires satisfying intricate testing requirements involving program states, execution paths, and assertions. Existing LLM-based approaches leverage program context, static analysis, and dynamic feedback but lack explicit tracking of individual testing requirements across iterations, potentially leading to redundant generation and unresolved testing objectives. We present TATG, a tracking-aware LLM-based unit test generation framework that unifies structural coverage and mutation-based fault detection. TATG introduces a structured objective representation capturing testing requirements derived from static analysis and dynamic feedback, enabling fine-grained tracking of their satisfaction status. It employs a two-stage workflow that first improves structural coverage and subsequently strengthens assertions through mutation-guided hardening. We evaluate TATG on 141 complex Java methods against state-of-the-art baselines, including KTester and PANTA. Results show average improvements of 22.15, 20.14, and 37.66 percentage points in line coverage, branch coverage, and mutation score, respectively. TATG also outperforms general-purpose coding assistants, including Codex and Claude Code, under the same open-weight model configurations, achieving higher average coverage and mutation scores while generating fewer tests and consuming fewer tokens. These findings highlight the value of explicitly tracking testing objectives for effective LLM-based test generation.
papers.title: TATG: Tracking-Aware Testing Objective for LLM-based Test Generation

papers.abstract: This study examines the impact of the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake on population distribution within Tokyo City. Using newly digitized census statistics and variation in fire damage across areas, I show that land readjustment under the reconstruction project reduced residential land in the burned area, and rents rose throughout the city, particularly in the burned area. Although residential floor area recovered through the construction of multi-story dwellings, the number of households in the burned area remained below its pre-earthquake level, whereas the population had returned to roughly its pre-earthquake level by 1935. The pre-earthquake zoning system had little effect, suggesting that post-disaster population distribution was shaped by market-based price adjustments rather than regulation. The population in the burned area thus reflected the net effect of two opposing forces: fewer households due to the loss of residential land, partly offset by more households per dwelling through lodging, and larger households through the inclusion of non-kin members, such as servants and employees.
papers.title: Urban Reconstruction and Population Redistribution: Evidence from Tokyo after the Great Kanto Earthquake

papers.abstract: Liquid democracy lets voters either vote directly or delegate their voting power to another trusted participant. It is often deployed in political parties, municipal participation platforms, and the governance of decentralized autonomous organizations. Existing approaches make delegations publicly visible as they form, which results in herding driven by popularity, makes coercion verifiable, and leaves the election fragile when popular delegates abstain. We propose a novel liquid democracy mechanism that removes these vulnerabilities, while keeping the tally fully auditable. Delegation choices are sealed with decentralized timed-release encryption, while they are formed and before revealed in full for tallying. Each voter determines ranked backup delegates together with a personal fallback ballot so that delegation failures do not result in abstaining. Experiments grounded in real-world voting data show that the mechanism keeps voting power dispersed, whereas transparent formation concentrates it into few hands. Strikingly, vote loss under targeted delegate failures falls from 26% to 3%.
papers.title: Resilient Liquid Democracy: Mitigating Voting Power Imbalances via Secure Delegation Networks

papers.abstract: Filtered vector search returns the nearest neighbors among the vectors that pass a predicate. The predicate is often selective: most tag queries of the Big ANN filtered track select less than 1% of YFCC 10M. Predicate-agnostic methods search one HNSW graph built without metadata and so take any predicate, but below a few percent selectivity they break down. ACORN-1 draws candidates only from passing neighbors and its recall collapses below 1%. HNSW keeps searching but spends about ef/s expansion cycles at selectivity s. We present RACORN-1, an extension of ACORN-1 that keeps its graph and filter-first traversal and adds Adaptive Search Fallback. When the two-hop expansion of a node falls short of a target, failing nodes enter the candidate queue as bridges, under a per-expansion budget, but never enter the result queue. RACORN-1 serves the selectivities ACORN-1 cannot: from 1% down ACORN-1 no longer reaches recall 0.9 at any ef, while RACORN-1 reaches 0.95 from 3% down on every dataset we sweep. It also reaches 0.9 on every natural filter that YFCC and LAION ship and on every conjunction and caption predicate we run, where ACORN-1 misses more than half. With a deadline equal to the time HNSW needs to fill its result queue, RACORN-1 returns the higher recall on all eight datasets at four selectivities. On eight indexes of 1M to 100M vectors, at 1% selectivity and recall 0.9 it is 1.3-8.4x faster than HNSW, and it is 2.2-10.5x faster under adverse correlation.
papers.title: RACORN: Robust Predicate-Agnostic Filtered Vector Search under Extreme Selectivity

papers.abstract: Empirical quantum-software papers often claim that one compiler produces smaller circuits, one optimizer is more reliable, or one ansatz achieves better solution quality. Such comparisons depend on benchmark scope, circuit construction, compilation, sampling, backends, noise models, optimizer choices, and resource budgets. Existing testing, benchmarking, and reproducibility methods help assess programs and experiments but do not directly audit whether the reported comparison is supported by the evidence available in the paper and artifact. We present CLAIMSTAB-QC, a source-bounded framework that records baselines, metric, relation, and admissible evidence; locks the audit design before outcomes are computed; and reports a scoped relation outcome or an explicit evidence boundary. Strict scalar-directional comparisons are classified as Sustained, Unresolved, or Not preserved within the locked audit scope. We examine 455 comparative claims from 119 quantum-software papers. A materialization gap emerges: 175 claims can be represented for audit planning, 79 become scalar-directional planning records, and 53 yield lockable audit or diagnostic designs, but only 8 expose enough matched evidence to audit the original comparison without proxy reconstruction. Among these 8, 2 are Sustained, 4 Unresolved, and 2 Not preserved. Controlled diagnostics over 24 benchmark-relevant quantum-workload comparisons further show that simpler checks can preserve apparent directions despite weaker support under locked designs. These results indicate that performance orderings should be reported with matched evidence sufficient to audit their stated scope.
papers.title: When A Beats B Needs Evidence: CLAIMSTAB-QC for Auditing Comparative Claims in Quantum Software

papers.abstract: Equal load does not mean equal decode latency in prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving. In bandwidth-bound decode, more distinct experts mean more weight loads and higher latency. We present ELDR, a lossless, expert-locality-aware decode router. Prefill signatures predict decode expert usage. Balanced $K$-means fits per-decoder centroids with background refitting. Locality-band routing selects the least-loaded worker among close matches. A block-granular cache keeps signatures exact under prefix caching. We evaluate ELDR in vLLM on up to 40 GPUs. Across three MoE models on 12 public task benchmarks and multilingual WildChat, it reduces median time-per-output-token (TPOT) by 5.4-14.5% on average across request rates and up to 17.8% over the best of four load-balancing baselines, preserving model outputs and token-to-expert assignments.
papers.title: ELDR: Expert-Locality-Aware Decode Routing for PD-Disaggregated MoE Serving

papers.abstract: Spin correlations are among the most fundamental quantum observables in many-body systems, yet they remain difficult to access experimentally in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Existing spin measurements, including hyperon polarization and vector-meson spin alignment, have revealed important single-particle spin phenomena, but genuine two-particle spin correlations in the produced hadronic system remain largely unexplored. Here we propose spin femtoscopy, a framework for accessing genuine two-particle spin correlations through spin-resolved femtoscopic measurements. The key principle is that different two-particle spin configurations can give rise to different femtoscopic correlation functions because of quantum statistics and spin-dependent final-state interactions. Using $ΛΛ$ pairs as a proof of principle, we exploit the self-analyzing weak decay of $Λ$ hyperons to construct spin-sensitive femtoscopic correlation functions with different singlet and triplet admixtures. We show that these observables provide experimental access to the spin-state populations of the pair and allow genuine spin correlations to be separated from spin-dependent femtoscopic mixing caused by quantum statistics and final-state interactions. This work extends femtoscopy from a probe of source geometry and final-state interactions to a framework for revealing the quantum spin structure of strongly interacting matter.
papers.title: Spin Femtoscopy: A Framework for Revealing Genuine Spin Correlations

papers.abstract: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
papers.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras

papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, defines a standardized interface for connecting large language models (LLMs) to external tools, data sources, and services. Within months of release, hundreds of community-built MCP servers appeared on GitHub, but no software-maintenance literature has yet described how the ecosystem is being structured in production. This industry experience paper catalogues five recurring MCP server architectural patterns observed across an enumerated corpus of fifteen independently developed servers (five production servers from the ANSYR voice AI platform plus ten public servers from the official MCP registry): Resource Gateway, Tool Orchestrator, Stateful Session Server, Proxy Aggregator, and Domain-Specific Adapter. Each pattern is described in the structured form established by Gamma et al.: context, problem, solution, and consequences. We also document four anti-patterns and a set of cross-cutting concerns around authentication, versioning, and observability. Quantitative evaluation contributes two measurements: inter-rater reliability of the taxonomy across two independent LLM raters on 54 held-out servers (Cohen's kappa = 0.76), which also localizes three pattern-boundary ambiguities; transport overhead measured end-to-end on loopback (stdio: 0.01 ms p50; streamable-http: 0.39 ms p50) and modeled for cross-host paths from same-region network baselines (~30 ms p50 baseline plus protocol overhead). Version 2 withdraws the tool-count analysis of version 1, whose numbers could not be traced to production records. Code, corpus, and prompts are released at https://github.com/rodriguescarson/mcp-patterns-icsme2026.
papers.title: MCP Server Architecture Patterns for LLM-Integrated Applications

papers.abstract: We study prophet inequalities for $n$ i.i.d. base rewards subject to multiplicative discounts across $S$ phases. For equal-length phases and a common discount factor $\widetildeγ$, we characterize the optimal competitive ratio of single-quantile policies as $n\to\infty$ with $S$ and $\widetildeγ$ fixed. The resulting sharp guarantee describes the dependence on the phase parameters: it recovers $1-1/e$ without discounting and approaches $1/2$ in the worst-case regime. We also establish a distribution-free comparison that bounds the discounted prophet by a fractional i.i.d. maximum with effective horizon $B$, the sum of the discount weights across all observations. The comparison yields acceptance probability $1/B$, determined only by the phase profile. This calibration attains the canonical optimum even among single-quantile policies that may choose their acceptance probability using the known base distribution. The comparison also gives guarantees for heterogeneous discounts and unequal phase lengths. A complementary optimal-stopping upper bound establishes the same limiting optimum of $1/2$ for arbitrary stopping rules in the canonical model. Finally, the same effective-horizon calibration sets acceptance probability $1-\widetildeγ$ under infinite-horizon geometric discounting. This explicit quantile rule attains Boshuizen's (1994) known optimal worst-case ratio $1/(1+\widetildeγ)$ without solving a Bellman equation.
papers.title: Effective Horizons for Prophet Inequalities with Discounted I.I.D. Rewards

papers.abstract: Operating envelopes (OEs) define the admissible active and reactive power injections of distributed energy resources while respecting distribution network limits. In unbalanced low-voltage feeders, OEs based only on voltage magnitude and thermal limits may overestimate available flexibility because they neglect power quality requirements. This paper develops a three-phase unbalanced AC optimal power flow framework to compute coupled active and reactive power OEs while enforcing limits on the voltage unbalance factor (VUF). It also proposes a fairness mechanism based on voltage sensitivities to allocate available flexibility among multiple photovoltaic (PV) units. The proposed mechanism is compared with lexicographic max--min fairness as a benchmark for equitable resource allocation. Case studies on unbalanced test feeders evaluate how VUF constraints change the feasible operating region of PV units. The results show how VUF constraints affect feasible flexibility and demonstrate that the proposed voltage sensitivity-based mechanism is nearly six times faster than lexicographic max-min fairness.
papers.title: Voltage Sensitivity-Based Fair Allocation of Operating Envelopes in Distribution Networks

papers.abstract: LLM agents are expected to act over multiple turns, using search, browsing interfaces, and tools to complete user goals. Yet not every goal is well specified or achievable in an available environment. In such cases, a reliable agent should recognize that further interaction is unlikely to help and abstain from additional tool calls. We define Agentic Abstention, the problem of deciding when an agent should stop acting under uncertainty. Unlike standard LLM abstention, which is usually evaluated as a single-turn answer-or-abstain decision, agentic abstention is a sequential decision problem: an agent can answer, abstain, or gather more information at each turn, and the need to abstain may only become clear after interacting with the environment. We study this problem across web shopping, terminal environments, and question answering, evaluating 13 LLM-as-agent systems and 2 agent scaffolds on more than 28,000 task instructions. Our results show that the main challenge is not only whether agents can abstain, but also when they abstain. Some agents never abstain when they should, while others do so only after many unnecessary interactions. This gap is especially large on tasks where the instruction appears feasible until the environment reveals otherwise (e.g., no valid result matches the instruction). We further find that model scale, reasoning, and agent scaffolding affect abstention in different ways, where larger or more capable models sometimes perform worse at timely abstention. Finally, we introduce CONVOLVE, a context engineering method for improving agentic abstention that distills interaction trajectories into reusable stopping rules. On held-out WebShop tasks, CONVOLVE substantially improves timely abstention without updating model parameters, raising Llama-3.3-70B's timely recall rate from 26.7 to 57.4. Our dataset and code are available at https://agentic-abstention.github.io.
papers.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?

papers.abstract: Secure multi-party computation (SMC) addresses the problem of jointly computing global functions of private inputs while revealing minimal information about individual data. Two prominent examples of SMC tasks are sealed-bid auction and secure multi-party summation. Existing schemes for quantum auction and quantum summation have largely been developed independently, motivated by distinct applications and employing different computational primitives. In this work, mutual reductions between the two tasks are established for single-item sealed-bid auctions with first-price payment. In one direction, an auction used as a black box computes a secure sum: each party bids a private random key drawn from its input, so the clearing price depends on the inputs only through their sum $S$. The reduction is perfectly private against colluding semi-honest parties and uses $O(S^2\log(1/δ))$ auction rounds, which is optimal, or $O(S\log(1/δ))$ under coherent access. It can be instantiated with an existing auctioneer-free quantum auction after a one-line change to its disjunction subroutine, which as published leaks occupancy counts. In the other direction, summation with randomized inputs yields threshold disjunctions, and a single search over composite keys locates the highest bid and a winner, revealing nothing else. Because each query consumes the bidders' encodings, a bidder can adapt its effective bid undetected, while a fixed query set restores sealed bidding. Combinatorial auctions and general payment rules lie outside this framework. On a superconducting processor, one instance of each direction is executed, recovering the winner for four-bidder instances with ties and the sum of private inputs from repeated auctions.
papers.title: On the generic structures of the protocols for quantum auction and quantum summation and their relation

papers.abstract: We investigate holographically dual descriptions of $(2+1)$-dimensional s-wave and p-wave superconductors in the framework of regularized four-dimensional Einstein-Lovelock gravity theories, incorporating higher curvature corrections beyond the Gauss-Bonnet sector. We first implement the 4D regularization of Einstein-Lovelock gravity with finely tuned coupling constants to include corrections up to any $K$th order in curvature. The bulk geometry is constructed from exact black-brane solutions characterized by the fine-tuned Lovelock coupling $α$ and the highest power of curvature in the Lagrangian K. We then analyze the condensation of scalar and vector operators dual to minimally coupled matter fields, focusing on two bulk-field mass prescriptions, which significantly affect the superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that higher curvature terms significantly modify the phase structure of both s-wave and p-wave systems and enhance the sensitivity of the condensates and critical temperatures to the gravitational couplings. In both cases, the critical temperature generally increases with the maximal curvature order K, leading to higher-$T_c$ phases compared to Einstein gravity, particularly for negative $α$. The coupling $α$ effectively governs the strength of higher curvature interactions in the bulk: positive $α$ suppresses condensation and lowers $T_c$, whereas negative $α$ enhances superconducting order and promotes higher-$T_c$ phases relative to Einstein gravity. We further study the optical conductivity and find that both the gap frequency and the ratio $ω_g/T_c$ exhibit a strong dependence on $α$ and $K$, deviating from the universal Einstein-gravity result. Higher curvature effects enhance the superconducting gap scale. Notably, the p-wave system shows a stronger sensitivity to the mass-fixing prescription compared to the s-wave case.
papers.title: Holographic $s$- and $p$-wave superconductors from the $4D$ regularization of Einstein-Lovelock theory

papers.abstract: Adapting CLIP for open-vocabulary video recognition necessitates a delicate balance between newly acquired video knowledge and the pretrained generalization. While existing studies pursue this generalization-specialization trade-off with additional regularizations or constraints, we argue that they overlook the deviation of representations beyond the fine-tuning data distribution, resulting in suboptimal adaptation effects. We believe such deviation is inherited from the inconsistency between the fine-tuning and evaluation objectives, where model optimization is restricted to the known training distribution but evaluated on unseen ones. In this paper, we introduce \emph{TACO}, a simple yet effective framework to mitigate the potential negative effects induced by this inconsistency. Our key insight is that adaptation should preserve OOD-relevant alignment beyond the training distribution. To this end, we propose \emph{Relative Structure Distillation}, which regularizes the relative geometry of the representation space and suppresses harmful alignment shift during training. We further decouple the representation space from the optimization space with a lightweight specialization projection, allowing task-specific adaptation without directly overspecializing the representations used at test time. \emph{TACO} establishes state-of-the-art performance on diverse benchmarks under cross-dataset and base-to-novel settings. Code will be released at https://github.com/ZMHH-H/TACO.
papers.title: TACO: Towards Task-Consistent Open-Vocabulary Adaptation in Video Recognition

papers.abstract: Perceiving physical contact is fundamental to dexterous manipulation. While robots often rely on dedicated hardware tactile sensors, humans exhibit a remarkable ability to infer contact by integrating visual information with an innate sense of their body's pose and movement. Inspired by this embodied perceptual skill, we investigate whether a robot can learn to infer contact from vision, an approach that also offers a scalable alternative to tactile hardware specifically for binary contact estimation, which faces practical challenges in cost, fragility, and integration. We present NoContactNoWorries, a transformer-based multimodal framework that fuses RGB-D vision with the robot's proprioception to infer binary contact states as a pseudo-tactile signal for hand-object interactions. We validate by training a single contact prediction model on multiple objects and show that the inferred contact signal supports downstream reinforcement learning agents for in-hand object reorientation, generalizing to novel objects. Experiments in both simulation and on a real-world robot validate our approach, highlighting the feasibility of inferring contact from vision and proprioception. Project Page: https://soham2560.github.io/no-contact-no-worries/
papers.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation

papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics with an explicit solvent resolves the hydrodynamic response of a Brownian colloid in bulk and near a rigid wall over acoustic, inertial, and diffusive time scales. Bulk spectra establish a continuum reference and reveal departures associated with discrete-solvent dynamics. Under confinement, thermal spectra provide a measurement of the space-dependent added mass, while velocity autocorrelations determine space-dependent, anisotropic hydrodynamic memory and diffusion. All together, these measurements connect the enhanced added mass and reduced mobility near a wall, and probe the discrete-continuum crossover.
papers.title: Broadband molecular dynamics simulation of confined Brownian motion

papers.abstract: Bayesian experimental design (BED) has traditionally been based on maximising expected uncertainty reductions from prior to posterior. A major shortfall of this approach is that it leads to doubly intractable objectives that are difficult to optimise, while customising them to particular downstream tasks of interest can also be difficult. Following first principles decision theory, we demonstrate that BED can alternatively be formulated in terms of an expected future loss (EFL) on downstream actions, providing a simple and naturally task-driven framework. Critically, we then show that all such EFLs can be rearranged into singly intractable objectives that can be jointly optimised with respect to both the design policy and a downstream action policy using stochastic gradients, an approach we refer to as ACTION-BED. This formulation further sidesteps the need for any explicit posterior or marginal likelihood estimation and is naturally implicit, requiring only the ability to sample from the joint model over model parameters and data, and evaluate the downstream loss function. It thus allows design policies to be learned more effectively, efficiently, and simply than existing methods, while providing easy customisation to different downstream tasks and losses.
papers.title: Action-BED: Task-Driven Bayesian Experimental Design with Singly Intractable Objectives

papers.abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been successfully applied in various power electronic systems owing to its high efficiency, scalability, and superior output performance. Although the half-bridge submodule (HBSM) is widely used in MMCs for its structural simplicity, it is incapable of handling direct-current (DC) short-circuit faults. The diode-clamp submodule (DCSM) addresses this limitation by providing DC fault ride-through capability. However, because its two identical capacitors are connected in series, the equivalent capacitance is halved. To overcome this drawback, an enhanced SM is proposed in this paper. For the same energy storage capacity, the proposed SM reduces the total required capacitance by 75% compared with the DCSM. In addition, the proposed SM requires one fewer diode than the DCSM, thereby lowering the overall MMC capital cost. The topology and the operating modes of the proposed SM are described in detail, and its functionality is experimentally validated. The results demonstrate that the proposed SM can suppress DC fault currents and restore normal operation without additional external protection devices.
papers.title: An Enhanced Submodule for Modular Multilevel Converters With DC Fault-Clearing Capability

papers.abstract: We derive a gauge-invariant clean-limit decomposition of the second-order dc nonlinear conductivity in multiband tight-binding systems within the velocity-gauge Keldysh Green's function formalism. In the constant-relaxation-time approximation, the dc response separates into four contributions with distinct lifetime $τ$ scalings and physical origins: the nonlinear Drude term $σ^{\mathrm{ND}}_{ijk}\proptoτ^{2}$, the Berry-curvature-dipole term $σ^{\mathrm{BCD}}_{ijk}\proptoτ$, the intraband quantum-metric-dipole term $σ^{\mathrm{intra\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\proptoτ^{0}$, and the interband quantum-metric-dipole term $σ^{\mathrm{inter\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\proptoτ^{0}$. The intraband term is a Fermi-surface dipole of the ordinary band quantum metric, while the interband term is written, in the present representation, as a Fermi-sea-type response involving a band-normalized quantum metric. Working entirely within the velocity-gauge Keldysh--Kubo framework, we show that all connection-dependent commutator terms generated in the band-basis expansion cancel exactly between the covariant-quantum-connection sector $σ^{\mathcal{C}}_{ijk}$ and the three-Berry-connection sector $σ^{\mathcal{T}}_{ijk}$, making the role of the Peierls contact velocity vertices $V_{ij}$ and $V_{ijk}$ explicit; a complementary projector-based derivation appears in Ulrich et al., Phys. Rev. B 113, L201107 (2026), and our Fermi-surface dc-limit expression agrees with that reference after accounting for index and convention differences. As a diagnostic illustration, we introduce a real two-band model in which the Berry curvature and hence the BCD response vanish identically while the intraband quantum-metric dipole remains finite, establishing a practical route to quantum-metric dc responses not reducible to the Berry-curvature-dipole mechanism.
papers.title: Second-order dc conductivity in the velocity-gauge Keldysh formalism: gauge-invariant decomposition into nonlinear Drude, Berry-curvature-dipole, and quantum-metric responses

papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement is a central resource for emerging quantum technologies, but its experimental certification usually assumes that prescribed quantum measurements can be realized exactly. This assumption becomes increasingly restrictive in high-dimensional systems, where accurate measurement control is more challenging. Here, we show that arbitrarily small, adversarially tailored measurement deviations can lead to the false certification of high-dimensional entanglement in systems that are, in fact, separable, with the effect becoming increasingly severe as the dimension grows. We experimentally demonstrate this across a broad range of dimensions using classical photonic states encoded in the spatial degree of freedom. We report false certification of several tens of entangled dimensions in systems spanning up to 61 dimensions while exploiting measurement deviations as low as 0.23%. Our results reveal how imperceptible invasive attacks can critically compromise high-dimensional entanglement certification, motivating the development of new certification methods robust to bounded discrepancies between theory and experiment.
papers.title: Imperceptible measurement deviations can fake high-dimensional entanglement

papers.abstract: Unanchored indirect treatment comparisons using single-arm evidence are increasingly used in health technology assessment (HTA) when anchored comparisons of randomized evidence are not possible. Existing population-adjusted methods, including matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC) and simulated treatment comparison (STC), are generally limited to pairwise analyses and typically estimate marginal effects in the comparator study population, which may differ from the decision-relevant target population. We propose multilevel unanchored meta-regression for single-arm indirect comparisons (ML-UMR-SA), a Bayesian outcome-regression framework for synthesizing individual patient data and aggregate data from single-arm evidence. ML-UMR-SA respecifies multilevel network meta-regression to pool absolute outcomes rather than relative treatment effects, jointly modeling individual- and aggregate-level data and linking aggregate outcomes through marginalization over study-specific covariate distributions, enabling estimation across multiple treatments, studies, and target populations. ML-UMR-SA distinguishes assumptions required to identify treatment effects from those required to transport results to target populations. Valid inference relies on strong and often unverifiable assumptions, particularly conditional constancy of absolute effects and cross-treatment identifying assumptions such as the shared prognostic factor assumption (SPFA). These requirements are made explicit within a Bayesian modeling framework that facilitates sensitivity analyses. In simulations without unobserved confounding, ML-UMR-SA produced low bias and nominal coverage for comparator-population effects. Transportability to alternative populations depended critically on identifying assumptions, whereas incorporating subgroup information restored near-unbiased estimation and nominal coverage.
papers.title: Anchors Away: Navigating Single-Arm Indirect Comparisons with Multilevel Unanchored Meta-Regression (ML-UMR-SA)

papers.abstract: It has been observed that the Universe is permeated by the cosmic photon background, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. We investigate the conversion of the photon background into gravitons in the presence of background magnetic fields in the Milky Way Galaxy and in blazar jets. We find that the resulting graviton background is dominated by the contribution generated in blazar jets. Importantly, this graviton background constitutes a graviton floor for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors searching for new physics, analogous to the neutrino floor.
papers.title: Graviton Floor

papers.abstract: Many societal decisions are settled by contests of persuasion. Conversational AI is a powerful new entrant in these contests, but whether it can out-persuade skilled and highly incentivized humans has remained unclear. Here, in a series of four preregistered experiments (n = 18,978 conversations from 6,923 people), we pitted AI systems against a range of human persuaders, including laypeople, winners of a separately preregistered four-round online persuasion tournament, professional canvassers, and world championship debaters. We found that AI systems were reliably more persuasive than expert humans, even when expert humans chose their issues, researched in advance, underwent hours of live, structured practice, and were incentivized with £1,000 cash bonuses. In a follow-up study, AI's advantage persisted after experts received a coaching tool that let them practice against the AI that beat them, review their performance history, and see what AI would have said at key moments. We found converging evidence that AI's advantage stemmed from rapidly deploying larger quantities of information: after coaching, expert humans could tie an AI constrained to respond at human speeds and with human-length messages. In a final study, we show that AI's advantage extends to consequential real-world behavior: AI was more than 3x more effective than professional canvassers from a UK fundraising firm at raising real-money donations to Save the Children. Together, these results establish that frontier AI systems out-persuade expert humans in text-based conversation, with significant implications for political communication.
papers.title: AI out-persuades expert humans in text-based dialogue

papers.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) enables efficient adaptation of large pretrained models to downstream tasks by parameterizing weight updates with low-rank matrices. In this paper, we investigate the limitations of the LoRA parameterization from a geometric perspective. Specifically, we show that when a full fine-tuning gradient is backpropagated to the low-rank matrices, it undergoes anisotropic scaling driven by their singular values. We argue that this phenomenon is undesirable because it distorts the full fine-tuning gradient by skewing it toward dominant singular directions while suppressing others. Our analyses demonstrate that anisotropic gradient scaling reduces the effective rank of the low-rank matrices' gradients and fails to provide the best possible alignment between the full fine-tuning gradient and its low-rank approximation in LoRA for arbitrary gradients, thereby exacerbating the gap to full fine-tuning. To address these limitations, we propose a new low-rank parameterization, SDS-LoRA, which Structurally Decouples Singular values from the backward pass. Our method ensures that the full fine-tuning gradient backpropagates only through the orthonormal bases of the low-rank matrices' subspaces, independent of their scales. Convergence analysis demonstrates that while LoRA's convergence rate degrades with the condition number of the low-rank matrices, that of SDS-LoRA remains independent of it. Experimental results across natural language and vision benchmarks show that SDS-LoRA improves loss convergence and reduces the gap to full fine-tuning, significantly enhancing adaptation performance. The code is available at https://github.com/JungHunOh/SDS-LoRA_NeurIPS2026.
papers.title: SDS-LoRA: Overcoming Anisotropic Gradient Scaling in Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.abstract: As AI moves into the physical world, from robots to environmental sensors to medical wearables, it increasingly relies on local inference to meet latency, communication, or privacy constraints. Optimizing models for heterogeneous edge hardware such as microcontrollers (MCUs) requires simultaneously satisfying hard physical constraints on memory, power, and temperature while preserving accuracy, a multidimensional optimization that is today performed manually by experts. We ask whether an LLM agent can autonomously navigate this complex, multi-turn pipeline guided by real hardware feedback, and introduce a hardware-in-the-loop agent arena in which the agent iteratively refines both model and firmware by compiling, flashing, and measuring on real hardware, enabling closed-loop optimization. Frontier models, including Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, fail entirely without hardware feedback (0% deployment success), whereas our hardware-in-the-loop formulation achieves the first successful deployment within three iterations and can surpass human expert results within seven. This agentic co-optimization achieves 250x compression for vision models with <3.3% accuracy loss and 400x for audio with <6% Feature Error Rate loss, enabling battery-free operation on a commercial MCU via solar harvesting. We demonstrate practical impact in two real-world systems: an elk-detection camera trap (96.7% accuracy) and a phonetic-transcription wearable (8.37% FER) for child development research.
papers.title: Embedded Arena: Iterative Optimization via Hardware Feedback

papers.abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion aims to integrate complementary modalities, while existing Euclidean methods impose rigid distance metrics that distort multi-modal interactions and parent-to-child semantic hierarchies. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a text-driven fusion framework empowered by hyperbolic manifold learning. During training, BLIP-extracted text prompts serve as topological anchors within the hyperbolic space, guiding vision-attribute alignment through hyperbolic embeddings that naturally accommodate varying semantic granularities. By exploiting the exponential volume growth dictated by the Poincaré ball's negative curvature, this approach seamlessly embeds hierarchical trees to encode coarse-to-fine semantics without metric saturation, while the vast peripheral space prevents texture distortion during cross-modal fusion. At inference, the fusion process autonomously adapts to input content using the learned text-attribute priors, completely eliminating the need for textual input. Experimental results show our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on benchmark datasets, with code available at https://github.com/Shaoyun2023/TEDFusion.
papers.title: Text-Driven Fusion for Infrared and Visible Images: Achieving Image Scene Adaptation on Hyperbolic Space

papers.abstract: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent channel flow at Re_tau,0 = 200 examine the modulation of the near-wall self-sustaining process under sinusoidal and shape-optimised spanwise wall oscillation, with the same peak wall velocity and oscillation period. At a period close to the reported sinusoidal optimum for the prescribed peak velocity, the shape-optimised waveform gives a relative increase of approximately 6% in gross drag reduction over the sinusoidal signal, at a higher actuation cost; it is therefore used as a probe of the physical mechanisms underlying drag reduction. Phase-resolved stresses, vorticity variances and component-enstrophy budgets quantify the concurrent action of two tilting paths for the wall-normal vorticity of the near-wall streaks: towards the streamwise direction by the mean shear, and towards the spanwise direction by the Stokes strain. The magnitude of the Stokes strain orders the two paths: the spanwise path prevails over most of the cycle, and the streamwise path only while the strain is small, around its change of sign. Within 5 <= y+ <= 12, under the interval criterion q = 0.5, the shape-optimised waveform holds the strain at a nearly constant level for about 2/3 of the cycle, against 1/3 for the sinusoidal waveform, and so approximately halves the duration of the Reversal interval. The mean-shear production of streamwise enstrophy occurs mainly during Reversal: for the shape-optimised waveform its conditional rate is higher in every interval, whereas its time average is 23% lower, as Reversal is shorter. The lift-up production of wall-normal enstrophy is lower at every sampled phase. These observations support a duty-cycle description of the near-wall activity, in which the duration of each interval and the production rate within it are distinguished.
papers.title: Duty-cycle modulation of the self-sustaining process by spanwise wall oscillation

papers.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence models grow in complexity, interpretability has become an indispensable tool for understanding, debugging, and controlling their computations. However, interpretability lacks general theories to deductively design interpretable methods. This gap between theories and methods results in a fragmented literature and inconsistent evaluation protocols. To fill this gap, we introduce the Standard Interpretable Model (SIM), a general theory that enables the deductive design of interpretable methods from first principles. Specifically, the SIM summarises, in a set of premises, what interpretability is for a target entity. From these premises, the SIM systematically derives interpretability symmetries and corresponding constraints. One can then build interpretable models by either introducing constraints in the optimisation problem or by compiling constraints into an interpretable architecture. The most important finding, both theoretical and empirical, is that full expressivity and interpretability symmetries can coexist in the same model, showing that the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability is an artefact of model design. We demonstrate this on language models (LMs), where SIM-based LMs match the performance of equivalent opaque LMs without making any compromise on interpretability. Beyond this, the SIM shows how to improve the interpretability of existing pre-trained models, highlights underexplored research directions, and unifies a discipline that has long been fragmented, offering pedagogical grounding for interpretability curricula.
papers.title: The Standard Interpretable Model: Design interpretable machine learning methods from elementary symmetries

papers.abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.
papers.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions

papers.abstract: $g$ mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron star systems are potential probes of internal stratification, superfluidity, composition gradients, and the equation of state. Although such weak dynamical tidal signatures are unlikely to be resolved with current detector sensitivities, third generation observations may make them accessible, in which case identifying the weak resonant phase shift would provide information beyond the bulk adiabatic tidal deformability. We build a four class dataset in an eccentric harmonic framework, containing point particle, adiabatic tide, resonant $g$ mode, and pure noise samples, and use Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) detector data to test whether this weak resonant phase signature can be identified from noisy time domain strain. The ET, CE, and ET+CE deep learning models reach accuracies of $0.650$, $0.809$, and $0.875$, respectively. On the same simulated samples, the matched filtering method reaches lower accuracies of $0.534$, $0.703$, and $0.718$. This result arises from the fact that the resonant correction manifests as a weak phase morphology difference superimposed on the adiabatic tidal background, whereas matched filtering is sensitive only to the overall similarity. Hence, in the presence of weak phase differences, the neural network employed for the classification task is better able to learn these local phase and morphology features from the complete time domain strain segment. The results indicate that joint third generation observations improve the identifiability of weak internal mode phase information.
papers.title: Identifiability of $g$ mode Resonances in Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars with Multidetector Observations

papers.abstract: We describe Chronos LTV, a system to measure the long-term impact of delays and other service defects on key business metrics. We use Markov decision processes to model customer interactions over time, and formalize our target estimand as the marginal policy effect with respect to moving the average delay rate. Given this setup, we show that we can identify long-term effects under a sequential unconfoundedness assumption where delays are as good as random given observed order characteristics; and can estimate these effects using a simple covariate-balancing algorithm.
papers.title: What is the Long-Term Value of Reliability?

papers.abstract: Robust inertial odometry is essential for various carriers when external sensing is unreliable. Learning-based methods reduce integration drift by capturing local motion priors, but these methods often remain tied to a particular carrier, limiting generalization across heterogeneous platforms. We present MosaicIMU, a carrier-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) pretraining-and-adaptation framework for generalizable neural inertial odometry. MosaicIMU uses a prototype-based router to compose carrier-specific expert features, decodes local velocity and uncertainty constraints, and integrates them with a history-aware EKF. For unseen domain adaptation, it freezes the pretrained base model and learns a new lightweight expert residual branch. For edge-deployment, it further reuses the router to select informative online samples for efficient incremental updates. Experiments show that MosaicIMU consistently outperforms learning-based baselines, reducing average ATE and RTE-10s by 40% and 34%, respectively. These results highlight that MosaicIMU provides a scalable pretraining-to-deployment paradigm for generalizable and adaptive neural inertial odometry.
papers.title: MosaicIMU: Composing Carrier Experts for Generalizable Neural Inertial Odometry

papers.abstract: Recognising intentions from continuous movement trajectories is an important problem in spatiotemporal data mining. This becomes difficult when behaviours change over time and their boundaries cannot be directly observed. Football provides a useful setting for studying this problem because tactical intentions emerge from the coordinated movements of multiple players during possession. Existing methods for match phase recognition often classify individual frames, use predefined spatial rules, or identify only selected tactical patterns. They therefore cannot fully describe continuous possession sequences in which tactical intentions change over time. We address this gap by treating the identification of the in-possession match phase as a hierarchical sequence segmentation task. The framework includes three tactical intentions (Invade Opponent Space, Keep Possession, and Scoring) and six phases (Build Up, Progression, Counter Attack, Maintenance, Sustained Threat, and Finishing). We propose a Temporal Graph Attention Network (T-GAN) that combines player interaction graphs, contextual features, and Transformer based temporal modelling. The framework was evaluated on seven Bundesliga matches using leave-one-match-out validation and compared with rule-based, Random Forest, GNN, and Transformer baselines at both frame and sequence levels. The results show that temporal modelling is important for coherent phase segmentation, while graph modelling provides additional value for transition phases such as Counter Attack. The framework provides an interpretable method for discovering intention based behavioural segments from continuous player tracking data and supports automated tactical analysis in football.
papers.title: Intention Driven Identification of In-Possession Match Phases in Association Football through Temporal Graph Learning

papers.abstract: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_θ$ and the time-ordered transform $R_θ$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.
papers.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths

papers.abstract: Reasoning-trained language models can select, zero-shot, a small set of relevant labels from thousands to hundreds of thousands of candidates. We ask how they do it mechanistically, and whether the mechanism can be distilled. We treat each decision as a token-level event scored by the model's own margin: the token that picks a coarse region of the label space, the tokens that pick a label within it, and the token where the output departs from a near-miss named earlier. Attribution, exact mean-ablation, knock-in and a null calibration give individual attention heads causal standing. On clinical coding of MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, with all 5,651 candidate codes in context, a small, global, phase-structured set of heads is necessary and sufficient on essentially every summary; distinct head families read the candidate region and the earlier near-miss, and blocking what they read removes their effect; for mentions elicitable in the reasoning, a disjoint mid-layer set makes the region elicitable several tokens before the code. The structure recurs in a second reasoner. We introduce MISTILL, which, unlike chain-of-thought distillation, also supervises the student's pooled attention at these decision events. Read on heads found after training, it nearly doubles the causal recovery of the contrastive decision in a cross-family student and adds a small, seed-stable gain in one that already carries most of it, with no detected task difference at matched precision; under matched selection it exceeds a frozen random-head pool on both recovery and task score. On two corpora with human-annotated evidence (one read zero-shot, one in domain), a MISTILL student's decision heads attend to each code's evidence more, and more specifically, than a chain-of-thought-distilled student's. A pre-registered evidence-flip test detected no improvement in evidence-dependent decisions through the tested routes.
papers.title: Characterize Then Distill: Mechanistic Reasoning in Large Output Spaces

papers.abstract: Safety-critical traffic scenario generation is essential for evaluating autonomous driving systems under rare but high-risk interactions. Existing diffusion-based methods offer strong controllability in closed-loop generation, but their iterative denoising process is computationally expensive and may accumulate sampling and guidance errors over long rollouts, causing unrealistic motion artifacts such as abnormal acceleration and off-road behavior. To address these issues, we propose RiskFlow, a closed-loop safety-critical traffic generation framework that reformulates future behavior generation as one-step flow transport in the action space during training. At test time, RiskFlow generates safety-critical interactions through a selective guidance procedure in which time-to-collision-based critical-agent ranking selects high-risk agents and an adversarial interaction objective directly refines their output actions. Vehicle-dynamics rollout and map-aware regularization then translate guided actions into feasible trajectories while discouraging off-road behavior. By intervening on selected agents in the output space, RiskFlow avoids repeated corrections of intermediate denoising states, thereby mitigating accumulated guidance errors and accelerating closed-loop scenario generation. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset under closed-loop evaluation show that RiskFlow achieves a strong adversariality-realism trade-off across multi-agent and long-horizon settings. Compared with representative baselines, RiskFlow consistently improves realism while maintaining competitive safety-critical generation capability, and substantially reduces inference time for evaluation.
papers.title: RiskFlow: Fast and Faithful Safety-Critical Traffic Scenario Generation

papers.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are widely used for mechanistic interpretability in large language models, yet their standard formulation assigns each latent feature a single decoder direction, implicitly assuming features to be one-dimensional. We show that this assumption can induce feature splitting when model features are multi-dimensional. Geometrically, accurately reconstructing a feature under a fixed co-activation budget can require exponentially many decoder directions as its dimension grows. From an optimization perspective, adding decoder directions can strictly lower the $\ell_1$-regularized population risk, even when a basis can already reconstruct the feature exactly. Motivated by these results, we introduce Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders (SASA), which replace single-vector decoders with learned subspaces, enforce sparsity through Top-$s$ group gating, and adapt group rank with nuclear-norm regularization. Under an idealized single-feature model, we prove that the SASA objective is minimized by a single group whose reconstruction map recovers the feature subspace. We also derive polynomial sample complexity bounds for subspace estimation within a group and a lower bound on the samples needed to observe every atom in a fixed fragmented dictionary. Experiments on GPT-2 and Mistral-7B show reduced absorption compared with SAEs. Matched-budget GPT-2 comparisons show lower absorption for concept families and more accurate prediction of their members using a small number of latent coordinates, at a reconstruction cost. The code is available at https://github.com/arshandalili/sasa.
papers.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability

papers.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) is important in biological, atmospheric, plasma, industrial, and astrophysical environments, where reliable electron-collision data support modelling charged-particle interactions with matter. Its well-known experimental properties make it suitable for assessing how the target electronic-structure description affects low-energy electron scattering calculations. In this work, NO properties were evaluated using B3LYP, M06-2X, PBE0, and $ω$B97X-D3, with basis sets ranging from minimal to quadruple-zeta quality. Bond length, dipole moment, ionisation potential, and polarisability were compared with experiment to assess the sensitivity of the target description to the functional and basis set. The aug-cc-pVQZ basis set was then used to generate target models for ab initio R-matrix calculations over 0.1--20 eV. The total cross sections show low-energy resonance features, with the strongest functional dependence around the broad peak near 0.8--1.0 eV. A sharper, higher-energy structure is also observed below 2 eV, shifting from 1.74 to 1.82 eV depending on the functional. Differential cross sections show modest functional sensitivity, with more noticeable angular differences at 7.5 and 10 eV. These results show that the DFT functional and basis set affect the target properties, with the resulting target description influencing low-energy electron-scattering observables of NO. The comparison supports $ω$B97X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ geometry optimisation followed by aug-cc-pVQZ target-property calculations as a practical protocol for R-matrix modelling of NO.
papers.title: Influence of DFT Functionals on Low-Energy Electron Scattering Cross Sections of Nitric Oxide

papers.abstract: Evaluating large language model (LLM) agents in multi-turn interactive environments is expensive and risky, as it requires online environment interaction. We propose ADWM (Autoregressive Diffusion World Model), an evaluation framework that estimates the performance of a new LLM agent policy purely from pre-collected trajectories. The core idea is to learn a latent diffusion world model that simulates how the environment responds to the evaluation policy, without ever executing it in the real environment. Existing diffusion-based OPE methods guide full trajectories in a single pass by jointly diffusing states and actions, an assumption that breaks down for LLM agents whose actions are discrete text that must be sampled from the policy after observing the environment. Unlike autoregressive world models that suffer from compounding errors, ADWM models each transition as an independent denoising process, enabling reliable step-by-step rollouts where the world model and agent alternate in causal order.
