This is a notable point of inefficiency, as learning additional parameters for the projectors increases training costs, only for them to be discarded immediately after training. We introduce RAPID (RAndomized Projection for Internal Distillation) a novel distillation methodology which eliminates the wasteful projection learning by leveraging randomized methods. RAPID utilizes an efficient transform construction based on the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma to compress the teacher representations into the student embedding space with strong theoretical guarantees of structural preservation. RAPID also employs a combination of exponential moving average (EMA) and homoscedastic uncertainty weighting in a novel multi-objective function designed for internal distillation. Our experiments in post-training for reasoning demonstrate that RAPID increases training efficiency by as much as 21.1% while maintaining performance comparable to existing methods.
papers.title: RAPID: Increasing Efficiency of Internal Distillation via Randomized Methods

papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P$^2$-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P$^2$-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P$^2$-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD.
papers.title: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors

papers.abstract: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping. Updating whole batched tensors rather than individual experts is what keeps Sonar-MoE fast, as it avoids a 20% to 72% slowdown while using the same memory. Sonar-MoE matches optimizer-in-backward over all parameters in memory and speed while still clipping the dense parameters.
papers.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training

papers.abstract: For an infinite Gaussian matrix with independent entries and doubly monotone variances, we identify its algebraic principal ideal by a deterministic shell profile. The exact boundedness condition also implies compactness. A lower singular-value estimate uniform in the mean gives an exact sum law under each fixed compact perturbation. Conditional products and spatial compression yield the corresponding classification for Gaussian evaluations of Hilbert two-forms. For Wiener area of covariance rank at least two, the generator is the covariance tail divided by its index. The area and covariance generate the same ideal precisely under regularity at infinity.
papers.title: Gaussian Matrices and Exterior Forms: Deterministic Principal Ideals

papers.abstract: Erdős, Rubin and Taylor asked whether $(a,b)$-choosability implies $(am,bm)$-choosability for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvořák, Hu and Sereni disproved this for $(a,b,m)=(4,1,2)$ and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. Following Jiang and Zhu, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)\le\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$. Here $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ is the choice number, and $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)$ is the strong fractional choice number, defined as the infimum of real $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$. We prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=3$ that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. This answers all these questions and gives a lower bound of $1/7$ on the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$ over planar graphs of choice number three. For all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable, using the six-vertex wheel $W_5$ as its core gadget. This gives the corresponding lower bound $1/3$ for each $k\ge4$. The case $t=0$ and $b=2$ recovers the main result of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni. Finally, for every integer $t\ge1$, there are a positive integer $k$ and a $k$-choosable graph that is not $(8k+4t-1,8)$-choosable. Thus the difference between the strong fractional choice number and the choice number is unbounded, even with multiplicity fixed at eight. We further prove $k+Ω(\log k)\le\sup\{\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G):\operatorname{ch}(G)=k\}\le2^{(1+o(1))k}$ as $k$ tends to infinity.
papers.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number by an arbitrarily large amount

papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguyên's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential $m$-positive classes and on the solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms

papers.abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
papers.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem

papers.abstract: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply. Agents frequently rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault; diagnosis varies 7x across models while prediction varies only 1.4x. Models also adopt surprisingly different experimental strategies, and greater exploration does not reliably yield better performance. In one failure mode, agents often perform the experiment needed to distinguish competing causes, but still fail to use the resulting evidence. LUCA turns these hidden failures into measurable behaviours, providing a controlled environment to study where experimental agents succeed and fail. Code: https://github.com/RelationRx/luca.
papers.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning

papers.abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.
papers.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library

papers.abstract: Humanoid rigging for modern characters with complex garments remains challenging due to the need for dense auxiliary skeletons and precise skinning control. Existing automatic methods primarily recover rigs from geometry, providing limited artist control over auxiliary articulation and often lacking explicit semantic or kinematic-chain structure for dense garment bones, leading to instability and weight bleeding. We present TailorRig, a framework that reformulates garment-aware humanoid rigging as a structured, controllable full-rig generation problem. This formulation shifts the goal from automatic rig recovery to artist-driven rig authoring, where both body-template compatibility and auxiliary articulation are explicit design choices. TailorRig exposes two explicit axes of artist control within a unified framework: a user-specified body skeleton template that preserves body-rig compatibility, and artist-provided semantic labels that drive an autoregressive generator to synthesize requested category-specific auxiliary bone chains. To robustly assign skinning weights under dense skeletal configurations, we further introduce a hierarchical chain-to-bone formulation: vertices are first associated to a kinematic chain, and bone weights are then refined within that chain, reducing weight bleeding between spatially adjacent but semantically unrelated structures. We evaluate TailorRig on a diverse set of characters and introduce Human-Mix, a large-scale dataset of over 38,000 humanoid models curated for garment-aware rigging. Experiments show that TailorRig improves skeleton accuracy, deformation stability, controllability, and practical usability over existing methods. Project page: https://xxxx0601.github.io/trig/ ; code: https://github.com/Tencent/TailorRig ; dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/tencent/TailorRig
papers.title: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging

papers.abstract: Financial document recognition is often assessed using character and word error rates, although these metrics do not express whether a system preserves the financial facts on which people and organisations act. This paper develops a human-centred, risk-constrained framework for evaluating financial document recognition as evidence recovery and decision support. It defines typed financial facts linked to visible source regions and separates verbatim transcription, deterministic normalization, and business interpretation. A layered quality model covers text, localization, layout, tables, fields, fact correctness, evidence grounding, uncertainty, robustness, and operational performance. Non-compensatory acceptance gates use one-sided uncertainty bounds for critical-field errors, preventing strong aggregate scores from masking failures in amounts, identifiers, signs, periods, or entity associations. Selective automation is formulated as a constrained routing problem that accounts for residual risk, human-review capacity, and review cost. The framework further specifies annotation and adjudication procedures, leakage-resistant benchmark partitions, statistical estimands, subgroup analyses, and a reproducibility card. Formal results establish the limitations of compensatory scoring, the non-zero upper risk bound after zero observed errors, and a loss sensitive decision rule for routing uncertain cases to human review. The contribution is theoretical and methodological; no new model, dataset, or empirical performance result is claimed.
papers.title: Human-Centred, Risk-Constrained Evaluation of Financial Document Recognition: Evidence, Critical Errors, and Selective Automation

papers.abstract: Semantic granularity, which refers to the levels at which visual representations organize image content into meaningful entities, is fundamental to image understanding. However, whether pretrained visual representations inherently encode semantic structures at multiple granularities remains poorly understood. This paper presents a representation-driven approach for discovering semantically meaningful image regions at different granularities through clustering of pretrained visual representations without semantic supervision. Specifically, we concatenate selected feature maps extracted from a pretrained visual model and apply a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based projection to derive pixel-wise principal representation map tensor (PRMs). The resulting PRMs captures latent semantic structures embedded in pretrained visual representations, making them accessible to subsequent semantic clustering. We then introduce the semantic continuity rate (SCR), based on the silhouette principle, to quantify the clustering behavior of PRMs at different candidate granularities. Furthermore, we analyze the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of SCR profiles to assess the PRMs suitability for discovering semantic-like meaningful regions at multiple granularities. Our results indicate that PRMs exhibiting a higher proportion of relatively high SNR values over an initial range of cluster numbers tend to yield more semantically meaningful regions across multiple granularities. We evaluate the proposed approach on the COCO-2017 and VOC-2012 validation datasets using Hungarian-matched intersection over union (HIoU). The results demonstrate competitive segmentation performance among the compared methods, supporting the feasibility of discovering useful semantic granularities through clustering PRMs without semantic supervision.
papers.title: Discovering Semantic Granularity in Images through Clustering of Pretrained Visual Representations

papers.abstract: Engineering drawings specify mechanical parts through orthographic projections. Recognizing which part a drawing depicts underlies part search, design reuse, and digitization, yet no public benchmark measures whether vision models can do it. We introduce Blueprint2CAD, a benchmark for drawing-to-render correspondence: given an orthographic line drawing and a shaded render, usually from another viewpoint, decide whether they show the same part. Its data layer, BlueCAD-30K, applies an open drafting pipeline to 29,925 Zero-to-CAD models, adding view-aligned renders, clean and dimensioned drawings from six viewpoints, and surface-type metadata. Frozen encoders retrieve the matching part from a 10,000-model gallery with up to 65% Recall@1 when viewpoints are known but 43% when they are not, and the four encoders we test lie within six points of each other: viewpoint, not backbone, is the bottleneck. Six zero-shot vision-language models reach only 0.52-0.67 verification accuracy, with model-specific Yes/No biases that chain-of-thought shifts but does not remove; a quick LoRA fine-tuning on in-domain pairs improves verification accuracy by a few points but sharpens these biases and leaves the viewpoint failure intact.
papers.title: Blueprint2CAD: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Engineering Drawing-to-CAD Render Correspondence

papers.abstract: Search-based planning remains a powerful policy improvement paradigm in reinforcement learning, driving milestone successes in discrete domains. However, extending this paradigm to continuous control exposes a structural mismatch: search evaluates a finite set of action candidates, whereas continuous RL typically relies on Gaussian policies. We show that winner-action distillation into a continuous Gaussian induces a \textit{projection error} and a stepwise variance-expanding gradient tendency when the selected action is sufficiently far from the current mean. Empirically, this tendency is associated with elevated terminal variance and a return gap on the evaluated tasks. To address this, we propose \textbf{Iterative Gumbel Planning (IGP)}. By adopting a per-dimension factorized categorical policy, IGP naturally aligns the policy support with the search candidates, eliminating the projection error and reducing the residual approximation to a bounded discretization error. To bypass the combinatorial explosion of high-dimensional discrete action spaces, IGP pairs Gumbel Top-$K$ candidate sampling with an MPPI-style multi-round iterative search to refine the policy at each state. Empirically, IGP achieves state-of-the-art aggregate performance and sample efficiency on DMControl and HumanoidBench. Furthermore, it produces more stable action sequences with lower temporal variance, demonstrating its practical potential for real-world robotic deployment.
papers.title: Iterative Gumbel Planning for Continuous Control

papers.abstract: Radiomic features derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are sensitive to scanners; therefore, they require harmonization across scanners. In a radiomic feature dataset, some batches may be severely underrepresented compared to the others e.g., the Erasmus Glioma Database, which may provide harmonized features biased towards the larger batches in the dataset. We investigated whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before empirical-Bayes ComBat estimation improves feature harmonization and reduces residual scanner association while retaining grade-related information. In this retrospective, the Erasmus Glioma Database included 733 eligible patients acquired at a single center across nine vendor-by-field-strength configurations. Structural MRI acquired at 1 T, 1.5 T, and 3 T; four structural MRI sequences were analyzed. From four structural MRI sequences, 428 features were computed using an IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics implementation. The sample sizes of some scanner batches were very small compared to others, which may produce unequal precision and shrinkage of batch-effect estimates. We proposed a data augmentation approach to overcome the limitation of ComBat. We provided exploratory evidence, along with confirmatory Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction to assess the proposed method. Before harmonization, 392/428 features (91.6%) differed significantly across scanner batches (median eta-squared=0.463). Standard ComBat reduced this to 13/428 (3.0%), whereas batch-augmented ComBat reduced it to 8/428 (1.9%); the median residual effect size was <0.001 for both harmonized conditions. Batch augmentation appeared to be a useful strategy to improve the performance of ComBat for feature harmonization under severe batch-size imbalance.
papers.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort

papers.abstract: The radius valley separating super-Earths from sub-Neptunes is understood as a signature of atmospheric mass loss, but the timescale over which it develops remains poorly constrained. We investigate the age evolution of the radius valley and the super-Earth population around FGK stars using gyrochronological ages. We select $746$ planets around $510$ FGK hosts with reliable gyrochronological ages between $0.1$ and $4$ Gyr. A subset of $581$ planets around $404$ hosts, for which detection and confirmation completeness can be characterised, forms the reference sample. We measure the valley morphology and its locus in the period-radius plane, and infer the intrinsic super-Earth fraction with a selection-conditioned mixture model that accounts for stellar-age uncertainties. The intrinsic super-Earth fraction increases primarily during the first $\sim2$ Gyr, with no significant subsequent evolution. An exponential approach-to-plateau model places $90\%$ of this increase within $1.9$ Gyr at $90\%$ credibility. The radius valley is consistently resolved from $\sim1.5$ Gyr onwards, with no significant evolution in its depth or width. Its minimum may shift from $\sim1.5\,R_\oplus$ before $\sim2$ Gyr to $\sim1.8\,R_\oplus$ at older ages, accompanied by a change in the shape of the super-Earth radius distribution, although these changes are only suggestive. This evolution is consistent with atmospheric loss continuing up to approximately $1$-$2$ Gyr for a fraction of planets. The tentative shift of the valley minimum towards larger radii may indicate that planets with more massive cores complete envelope loss later, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish between atmospheric-loss mechanisms.
papers.title: Tracking the evolution of sub-Neptunes. II. The radius valley on gyrochronological ages

papers.abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, $P_g - b_g$, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM). The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or, in simulation, from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a $g\times g$ map takes $1 + 2g^2$ runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9% (one seed), as occlusion and gradient $\times$ input do, while plain gradients remove much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at one wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask computed classically before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and $2\times2$ maps of the filtered input of 30 test pictures drawn at random in advance, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones ($r = 0.88$; standard estimator 0.82). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.
papers.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist crowdsourced fact-checking, yet evaluations focus on individual annotations. A correction's reach and reception depend on visibility, audience responses, and platform policies. We introduce correction context understanding: assessing corrective content, interpreting audience responses, and reasoning about platform dynamics within a shared environment. We build NoteHabitat from 36 months of Weibo Annotations data, linking 102,994 posts (42,853 annotations), 431,407 comments, and five policy events. Evaluating diverse model families across seven tasks spanning content, interaction, and management reveals three gaps. Annotation quality correlates only weakly with engagement ($ρ=0.068$), while four zero-shot LLMs systematically underrate quality relative to human judgments, especially evidence support and objectivity. Models also miss toxic comments supporting corrections (36.4% average recall across ten models). At the platform level, LLMs partially predict policy-associated outcome directions, but LLM-guided simulations poorly reproduce daily activity. Cross-group analyses expose blind spots tied to contribution types and reader stances that aggregate scores conceal. Reliable fact-checking AI must understand the note, the conversation around it, and the platform in which both unfold.
papers.title: No Note Is an Island: Probing LLMs' Understanding of Crowdsourced Fact-Checking Environments

papers.abstract: Navigation world models predict future observations conditioned on navigation actions to support planning, but their generalization across real-world environments remains constrained by the limited coverage of action-labeled data. Action-free navigation videos provide diverse visual experience, yet lack the recorded actions required for action-conditioned training. We introduce OpenNWM, a generalist navigation world model with latent action pretraining. It learns universal latent actions from large-scale action-free videos through visual prediction pretraining, and further aligns them with physical motions via action-conditioned post-training. To support video pretraining, we curate NavAnywhere, a large-scale action-free navigation video dataset comprising 17.5 million visual observations from 15 heterogeneous sources. It captures navigation by ground robots, humans, and drones, with diverse viewpoints and motion patterns across five broad scene types: residential areas, public and commercial spaces, urban settings, parks, and natural landscapes. Experiments demonstrate improved visual prediction on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, together with improved navigation performance. These results show that latent-action pretraining enables diverse, action-free videos to improve dynamics learning and generalization for open-world navigation.
papers.title: OpenNWM: A Generalist Navigation World Model with Latent Action Pretraining

papers.abstract: Registering intraoperative Ultrasound (US) bone-surface point clouds to preoperative Computed Tomography (CT) models can support radiation-free orthopedic navigation. Differences in imaging physics produce distinct surface sampling patterns, complicating cross-modal feature matching. Bone strongly reflects ultrasound and casts an acoustic shadow, so US captures only the probe-facing bone surface and leaves most CT points unmatched. This partial coverage makes correspondences ambiguous on near-symmetric bones. We propose CUFormer, a modality-aware registration framework. We introduce a Modality-Aware Transformer (MAT) that encodes input modality through identity embeddings and updates features through modality-specific adapters within a shared geometric matcher. We model imaging visibility and use predicted reference-side visibility to weight coarse and fine correspondences. CUFormer achieves the lowest mean registration errors among evaluated methods on two CT-US datasets, UltraBones100k and UltraBonesHip, and the CT-RGB-D dataset SpineDepth. On UltraBones100k, it reaches mean rotation error 4.53$^\circ$, translation error 3.19\,mm, and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) 2.54\,mm, reducing RMSE by 65.8\% relative to the best-performing baseline by this metric. These results demonstrate CUFormer's effectiveness in aligning partial bone surfaces with preoperative CT across anatomical sites.
papers.title: CUFormer: Modality-Aware CT-Ultrasound Point Cloud Registration for Orthopedic Navigation

papers.abstract: We prove a mean value theorem on the distribution of smooth numbers in two simultaneous arithmetic progressions, with generalizing a result of Drappeau. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $(\log x)^C<y<x^{1/C}$ for a sufficiently large $C$. Our result implies that $y$-smooth numbers are well-distributed in the residue classes of a fixed integer $a$ on average over moduli $\leq x^{5/9-\varepsilon}$ and $\leq x^{153/256-\varepsilon}$ for each $|a|\leq x$, which improves Drappeau's range $\leq x^{6/11-\varepsilon}$. As an application, we show that a positive proportion of $y$-smooth numbers $n\leq x$ satisfy $\min(P^+(n-1), P^+(n+1))>x^{407/720}$.
papers.title: Smooth numbers in simultaneous arithmetic progressions

papers.abstract: A language model that learns a new fact by fine-tuning can repeat it but cannot reason with it: taught that a person is a citizen of a new country, it still cannot say, without chain-of-thought, who the head of state of that person's country is. This two-hop curse is widely treated as a reasoning deficit, and the strongest knowledge editors answer it with synthesized reasoning data. We show that the reasoning is intact and the writing is wrong. Fine-tuning writes a new fact as an answer to be said, whereas the second hop reads the bridge ("that person's country") as an entity, from the middle layers on: patching the model's own representation of the entity into the bridge at those layers largely restores the second hop, yet after fine-tuning the bridge there is no closer to the new entity than before the edit. We therefore propose read-equivalent writing (Legible): one loss term makes the bridge phrase, at the layer where the second hop finishes reading it, match the model's own reading of the new entity, and keeps the same relation's other subjects unchanged. Phrases and targets come from the edited model itself, and no multi-hop training data is used. Across Qwen2.5, Llama-3 and Qwen3, Legible (I) composes learned facts more often than the model composes its own knowledge, on MQuAKE's two-hop-curse questions; (II) reaches 1.8-2.6x the bridge accuracy of CaKE, whose reasoning data composes no better than plain fine-tuning, and has the best average over composition, accuracy and locality against four families of writers; and (III) lifts the curse on RippleEdits, on the benchmark of Balesni et al., who named the curse, and at 14B.
papers.title: Write Facts the Way Models Read Them: Lifting the Two-Hop Curse

papers.abstract: Through nine nanoGPT experiments, we established training-learning-inference relations: realized updates elicit state-dependent finite-amplitude responses; learning persistently reorganizes distributed functional support, with target-specific readout-boundary crossings determining capability transitions; inference recruits learned support without changing the learned state. Factors identified in the fifth experiment yielded a direct predictor of post-update capability transitions, achieving 91.43% accuracy and 91.49% four-way macro recall across 5,088 targets. We tested these relations and prediction across five additional neural architectures. In a seventh system, concentrated correct feedback eroded previously mastered skills; rebalanced feedback restored their accuracy from 70.31% to 99.48%. Linking inference consequences to subsequent training closes these relations into unified training-learning-inference-reinforcement dynamics. We subsequently established a unified system of dynamical equations, used it to reconcile positive and negative findings across existing research, and derived mathematical relationships in other neural-network theories using only the assumptions of the original studies.
papers.title: Unified dynamics of training, learning, inference, and reinforcement in neural networks

papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent settings, exhibiting emergent collective behaviors, yet the role of curiosity as a driver of such dynamics remains understudied. We introduce CuriousTogether, a framework evaluating curiosity-driven multi-agent LLM interactions across three complementary dimensions: novelty-seeking, epistemic and social curiosity. Across eight tasks spanning reasoning, creative generation, and social bias mitigation, curiosity-guided multi-agent settings yield improvements over non-curious ones on seven out of eight tasks, with gains of up to 20.6% in story generation (semantic diversity) and a 14.9 pp reduction in stereotype rates. Furthermore, country-conditioned cultural grounding show benefits for story generation and social tasks, but can hurt precision-oriented reasoning. Finally, we show that inference-time multi-agent curiosity-based approach offers favorable quality-token trade-offs, compared with single-agent baselines. Together, these findings support curiosity-guided interaction as a practical mechanism for improving multi-agent collaboration, with downstream benefits for reasoning, creative, and societal tasks.
papers.title: CuriousTogether: Implications of Curiosity and Cultural Grounding in Multi-Agent LLM Interactions

papers.abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated $π_{0.5}$-based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. It also improves performance on RoboTwin 2.0 and raises the average success rate across four real-world bimanual tasks by 20.8 percentage points compared with $π_{0.5}$.
papers.title: Vision-Language Models Are Joint Denoisers in Robotic Action Generation

papers.abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph G is a set S of vertices such that any two vertices of S are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in S, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $χ_μ(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition V(G). Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter d, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. More generally, for all fixed $k\ge2$ and $d\ge2$, it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le k$ for graphs of diameter d. The proof rests on a reformulation of $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the 2-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from 2-colourability of 3-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.
papers.title: Mutual-visibility k-colouring is NP-complete for every fixed diameter

papers.abstract: Option desks adjust crypto option quotes into price surfaces that remain within bid-ask intervals and satisfy standard no-arbitrage restrictions across strikes before computing Greeks, hedge quantities, or risk measures. For the same quote panel, however, these constraints may admit multiple such surfaces, which we call admissible repairs, with different downstream outputs. We define the resulting variation as repair risk and propose repair-risk validation, a matched framework for quantifying dispersion in Greeks, hedge quantities, and risk measures. The mechanism is finite-difference amplification: two admissible repairs within price distance $\varepsilon$ can differ in local normalized-strike curvature by $4\varepsilon/h^2$, where $h$ is local normalized-strike spacing. We evaluate repair risk on Deribit BTC and ETH option chains, using $L_1$ and $L_2$ projections of midpoint prices onto the same admissible set as matched controls. Across 108 matched evaluations spanning 18 sampled calendar months, the median 90th percentile of the scaled spot-gamma gap for $L_2$ versus the $ρ=10$ smoothness-penalized repair is nearly twenty times the matched $L_1$--$L_2$ control. We also instantiate NN-Proj, a neural-projection repair, to test whether learned repairs exhibit repair risk. Despite good held-out fit, its downstream outputs remain distinct from those of classical repairs. Across five seeds with the same training window and architecture, its curvature dispersion exceeds the matched $L_1$--$L_2$ control in 17 of 18 months ($p=1.45\times10^{-4}$). For a USD 1 million risk reversal, switching from $L_2$ to the $ρ=10$ repair shifts the median 90th-percentile hedge notional by 18.62 basis points of gross spot notional. VaR-style estimates also exhibit greater dispersion across repairs. The repair rule is therefore part of the risk model, not merely a feasibility check.
papers.title: Quantifying Repair Risk in Crypto Option Surfaces

papers.abstract: We test whether Koopman structure helps a differentiable world model used to train a simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tracking policy by backpropagation through imagined rollouts, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train policies; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the accuracy cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the dynamics' curvature in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only tested online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, abandoning the structure. For this use, the MLP world model remains the better choice.
papers.title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking

papers.abstract: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle Aω,ω\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.
papers.title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators

papers.abstract: We estimate the integral curve of an unknown vector field from noisy tangent vector field on a known compact Riemannian manifold. We consider two sampling settings: independent observations at random locations that have already been collected, and a fixed response budget that allows subsequent locations to be chosen using pilot information. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the passive kernel estimator has curve error of order $n^{-2/(d+3)}$ in probability, with sample size $n$ and manifold dimension $d$. Its functional central limit theorem has a limit characterized by a linear stochastic differential equation. For active sampling, an independent pilot directs one new batch of measurements to neighborhoods of the target curve. Under localization, smoothness and design conditions, this concentration yields expected maximum curve error of order $N^{-1/2}$, including the pilot in the total response budget $N$. Both methods provide simultaneous geodesic confidence tubes with asymptotically exact coverage under mild conditions. Simulations show narrower active tubes in most reported settings, with improved small-sample coverage in some three-dimensional examples. Ocean-drifter observations illustrate mean-flow reconstruction on the sphere, and a canopy-flow LDA application uses retrospective active sampling to quantify lateral and vertical departures of local mean streamlines.
papers.title: Sampling Design and Confidence Tubes for Integral Curves on Riemannian Manifolds

papers.abstract: Does eliciting five weighted estimates within a single response consistently improve numerical judgments? We compare direct and multi-estimate elicitation across anchoring, hindsight, base-rate, conjunction, and status-quo/default tasks in six frozen configurations. Each configuration contributes 618 admitted development units and 3,702 admitted formal units; the six-configuration formal cohort contains 22,212 units, including 21 missing outcomes. Of 45 preregistered confirmatory tests across five configurations, 12 reject on complete cases and 11 retain directional confirmation after the prespecified missingness-protection rule. Only one adjusted bound exceeds its smallest effect size of interest: gpt-oss-120b shows a 10.68-percentage-point increase in post-outcome confirmation error under multi-estimate elicitation (worst-case estimate 10.04 points). The remaining ten retained effects have sub-threshold point estimates; non-rejection does not establish equivalence. Joint presentation lowers signed conjunction excess in four confirmatory configurations, but this comparison changes both constraint visibility and call structure. Flash-high combines two disjoint execution-window batches under an approved continuation protocol, preserving their identities and non-causal interpretation. Post-hoc candidate-spread associations across all six configurations remain in-sample and require independent predictive validation. The completed cohort provides no evidence for uniform debiasing by multi-estimate elicitation. Materials: https://github.com/asj252/llm-judgment-studies
papers.title: Multi-Estimate Elicitation Does Not Uniformly Debias Language Model Judgments

papers.abstract: Gradient imperfections disrupt the encoding benefits of long-readout imaging applications on high-performance systems. Currently, external field monitoring hardware provides the only reliable solution for general spatial-temporal gradient characterization. We present FESTiVE, a data-driven alternative to higher-order field monitoring. FESTiVE leverages parallel imaging to both implicitly model and explicitly recover field imperfections. Using a fast k-t mapping calibration scan, FESTiVE formulates a time-varying GRAPPA problem which maps k-space data corrupted by a time-varying gradient imperfection against a clean reference. This mapping is represented compactly with an implicit neural representation, from which the spatial-temporal fields are recovered in image space using coil sensitivities. In phantom, FESTiVE produces comparable field measurements to a Skope field camera across multiple non-cartesian 2D acquisition strategies and gradient specifications. In vivo, FESTiVE achieves state-of-the-art image quality for a high-performance diffusion spiral protocol on the head-only MAGNUS 3T, where higher-order phase imperfections are significant. At 7T, on the head-only Siemens TerraX system, FESTiVE enables 300μm spiral imaging where conventional field camera-based approaches fall below probe dephasing limits. In conclusion, FESTiVE enables robust high-resolution non-cartesian imaging on high-performance gradients, characterizing gradient imperfections using parallel imaging rather than field monitoring hardware.
papers.title: FESTiVE: Self-calibrated Spatial-temporal Gradient Characterization for Non-cartesian Imaging on High Performance Systems

papers.abstract: We study how the layers in deep neural networks (NNs) converge, using Wilsonian Renormalization-Group (RG) ideas to organize the spectral picture. During training, these layers often develop heavy-tailed power-law (PL) spectra, and the strongest checkpoints often appear near the PL exponent $α\approx 2$. This pattern raises a simple question: why should this value mark a well-trained layer? The answer is both statistical and physical. Our statistical hypothesis is that $α=2$ marks the boundary between stable if not optimal learning and overfitting via non-self-averaging. The physical answer is that the same value makes the spectral energy gain scale evenly across logarithmic spectral scales, which is the proposed Wilsonian marginal condition. We then apply the ERG trace-log condition, the proposed SETOL theory, which we justify by taking volume-preserving, scale-invariant transformations to remove arbitrary layer scale along the proposed RG flow. The resulting spectral RG flow connects the HTSR and SETOL theories to optimizers such as Muon, and motivates a new optimizer extension, WW-PGD. Together, these results point toward a spectral Renormalization-Group view of learning, in which NNs may approach shared spectral structure in the settings studied here.
papers.title: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning

papers.abstract: Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. Understanding how the deployed model succeeds and fails can steer subsequent data collection towards patching failures and reinforcing successes. However, robot deployments create large volumes of high-dimensional rollout data, which is challenging to understand and confidently ground data collection decisions in. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. We construct the graphs by learning to identify similar behavior modes across rollouts, connecting the behaviors temporally, and finally linking them to outcomes. In a user study on three real-world tasks, where participants analyzed rollouts to choose a data collection strategy, 16 of 18 preferred behavior graphs to rollout videos, reaching comparable conclusions with 40.3% lower perceived temporal demand and 37.6% lower effort. Beyond interpretability for deployment data, behavior graphs are capable progress predictors: across 43 datasets, they improve the rank correlation between predicted progress and true temporal order by 22.9% and reduce mean absolute error by 53.5% relative to the strongest baseline. As the number of deployed robots grows, behavior graphs lend structure to high-dimensional policy rollouts and make deployment data easier to interpret and reason about.
papers.title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data

papers.abstract: Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise. We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. Physical disguise, however, can bypass both a camera check and a radar presence check. To evaluate defenses, we develop a hybrid replay protocol from automatic identification system (AIS) tracks that combines recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack run-ins. We find that for recreational-labeled vessels attacking via direct run-in within 4 nautical miles, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% at 15-20 knots, compared with 12% for a track-only speed check. The checks are complementary on off-axis approaches, constraining the attacker to remain below both thresholds and extending the time required to reach the asset. Flagging on either check has a 4.9% held-out false-alarm rate overall and 12.3% on recreational traffic. The replay-based evaluation protocol supports comparative test and evaluation of defense methods.
papers.title: When appearance and motion disagree: evaluating class-motion consistency against disguised uncrewed surface vessels

papers.abstract: Dense labels of the aorta in CT are slow to draw, and the public aortic CT datasets that could stand in for them each label different structures under their own conventions. Large language model (LLM) agents can now write code and read images. We asked whether such a model labels these scans better as a free-form agent that writes its own segmentation code, or inside a harness, where an automated pass labels the scan and the model reviews the result. We built a harness, Taurus, and compared it with free-form agents by blind label recovery: we withheld the human labels of six public datasets (939 volumes) and scored every approach against each dataset's own classes. In the first version of Taurus, the model's review raised the primary metric on only two of six datasets, by less than the noise between two reviews of the same case. A free-form agent running Claude Opus 5.5 scored higher on most datasets. Moving what the free-form agents did well into the automated pass then carried most of the gain on 38 held-out cases. The final version smooths the label surfaces with a fixed rule and checks for the large errors the automated pass tends to make, such as an aneurysm drawn to half its size. Each check that fires puts a multiple-choice question to the model, with candidate corrections drawn on the scan. It matched the surface smoothness of the human references, and in the primary metric we found no difference from the free-form Opus agent, at under half its cost, $1.22 against $2.71 per case. Most of what made Taurus competitive came from the harness and its automation rather than from the language model itself. Taurus shows that this kind of annotation can be automated, so that expert time can move from drawing labels to checking them.
papers.title: Taurus: LLM-in-the-Loop CT Annotation Matches Coding Agents at Half the Cost

papers.abstract: Egocentric observations provide a robot-centric view of manipulation processes, capturing contact interactions and object-state changes that are important for visuomotor policy learning but difficult to observe from external cameras. However, collecting such data at scale remains expensive due to additional hardware requirements and platform-specific deployment costs. Synthesizing egocentric observations from large-scale exocentric manipulation videos provides a scalable alternative. However, existing methods struggle to synthesize physically consistent and policy-relevant egocentric videos under substantial viewpoint transformations, severe occlusions, complex object interactions, and inherently sparse observations from available exocentric viewpoints. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/xueha0/AuroraWorld
papers.title: AuroraWorld: Structured 4D World Modeling for Exo-to-Ego Video Generation in Robot Manipulation

papers.abstract: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. We show that at a fixed frequency, the wave cross section diverges in the forward direction as $θ^{-4}$ in any dimension, with a coefficient fixed by the mass, while the steeper classical law $θ^{-(D-2)^{2}/(D-3)}$ appears only at larger angles and higher frequencies. The charge parameter decreases the critical and the glory impact parameters and widens the glory fringes, and in higher dimensions, the glory pattern has fewer and wider fringes and a weaker backward intensity. For the matched configurations studied here, backward intensity and low-frequency absorption provide the clearest differences, while the intermediate-to-high-frequency spectra are close.
papers.title: Scattering of massless scalar waves by higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics

papers.abstract: The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma^3, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.
papers.title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films

papers.abstract: We study polarization-resolved high-harmonic generation in a laser-driven two-leg Su--Schrieffer--Heeger ladder with asymmetric dimerization under periodic boundary conditions. A field linearly polarized along the ladder can generate both longitudinal and transverse radiation, whose harmonic content is controlled by lattice symmetry and electronic filling. Using symmetry analysis of the time-dependent density matrix, we show that reflection symmetry enforces odd-order harmonics in the longitudinal response and, when the transverse response is nonzero, even-order harmonics in the transverse direction. At half filling, an additional anti-unitary symmetry relating the occupied and empty bands suppresses the transverse current completely. A unitary chiral symmetry in the clean ladder relates the same bands but fails to enforce this cancellation, showing that band swapping alone is insufficient: the suppression requires both a density-matrix constraint that persists during the driven evolution and the appropriate transformation of the transverse-current operator. Moving away from half filling lifts this cancellation and allows transverse emission, while the reflection selection rule remains whenever reflection symmetry is preserved. Numerical calculations at quarter and half filling, combined with onsite potentials that selectively break the relevant symmetries, confirm these two distinct mechanisms. Thus, reflection symmetry determines which harmonic orders occur, whereas the interplay of anti-unitary symmetry and filling controls whether the transverse HHG channel is present at all.
papers.title: Switching off a high-harmonic polarization channel by anti-unitary symmetry

papers.abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(χ_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasová, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.
papers.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers

papers.abstract: Terminal feedback in multi-turn agent training leaves both rollout allocation and local credit underdetermined. Dynamics-Predictive Sampling (DPS) [9] provides a task-level predictive sampling reference, but interactive agents also need to choose which visited states merit further continuations. We introduce TSBPO with two method components. A lightweight, fine-grained Root/Branch budget allocator distributes factual rollouts across tasks and additional suffixes across replayable states using likelihood-fitted estimates of terminal-outcome contrast. On the resulting physical rollout trees, a tree-aware step-level credit assignment algorithm compares immediate sibling segments and assigns their local outcome contrasts to the turns they contain. Exact task/observation groups provide a complementary step term. The allocator selects what to sample; observed outcomes determine the subsequent credit. With a Qwen2.5-1.5B actor, fixed checkpoints attain 97.79% seen and 96.64% unseen stochastic success on ALFWorld, and an 81.07% per-episode success rate over six stochastic episodes for each of the 500 WebShop test goals. At the WebShop update-100 checkpoint, removing the observation-group step term yields 75.93% under the same evaluation. These results describe the evaluated training configurations on two interactive benchmarks.
papers.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents

papers.abstract: Many kinds of generalised syntax, including internal categories, T-categories or polynomial monads, arise as monads in bicategories of a certain flavour: maps are some kind of span, and composition is some kind of pullback. We explain the pattern behind these similarities: each bicategory is stitched together from two simpler pieces by a distributive law, where the distributivity is governed by pullback. A key novelty is in the kind of distributive law we consider; where Rosebrugh and Wood considered distributive laws between categories, we instead consider pseudo-distributive laws between double categories. A key construction, drawing on work of Weber, obtains such a distributive law from a so-called co-crossed double category: one whose codomain functor is a fibration, and whose cartesian cells are stable under horizontal composition. We show the horizontal Kleisli double category of a monad T is co-crossed just when T is cartesian, and that the composite double category recovers T-spans; that the double category associated to an identity-on-objects functor is co-crossed just when that functor is a calibration in the sense of Bénabou; and that Street's calibrated bicategories yield co-crossed double categories in a similar manner, recovering the double category of polynomials of Gambino--Kock.
papers.title: Composing Double Categories

papers.abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.
papers.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering

papers.abstract: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.
papers.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect

papers.abstract: Stellar bars redistribute gas and angular momentum in disk galaxies, but whether they mainly change the amount or the spatial organization of recent star formation remains uncertain. We use archival HST/WFC3 F275W imaging to study 70 barred galaxies and 95 unbarred control galaxies matched in stellar mass, optical color, redshift, and F275W background noise. A uniform dendrogram-based procedure identifies 95,486 UV-bright star-forming clumps. We compare their radial and azimuthal distributions, central F275W emission, and luminosity and size distribution functions. Relative to their controls, barred galaxies show a deficit of clumps at intermediate radii broadly corresponding to the bar region, followed by a local recovery near the bar ends. Their clumps are also preferentially concentrated along the bar major axis. These spatial differences are stronger in high-mass galaxies. Normalized bar length is more closely associated with the radial redistribution and central F275W concentration than bar ellipticity, although its relation to the azimuthal distribution is less uniform. When galactocentric radius is normalized by bar length, the recovery occurs near $R/R_{\rm bar}\sim1$, indicating that the bar sets a characteristic scale for the redistribution. Despite these spatial differences, barred and control galaxies have broadly similar clump luminosity and size distribution functions. Our results suggest that stellar bars mainly reorganize where recent star formation occurs, rather than substantially altering the observed luminosities and sizes of individual UV clumps, and that this effect depends on galaxy mass and bar extent.
papers.title: Stellar Bars Reshape the Spatial Distribution of UV-bright Clumps in Nearby Galaxies

papers.abstract: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of $n$-complexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
papers.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds

papers.abstract: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $μ^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including the exciting prospect of measurements of the Higgs boson self-interaction, and is followed by a presentation of the FCC-$μe$ layout -- from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$μe$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.
papers.title: FCC-μe: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN

papers.abstract: We develop a state discrimination approach to unassisted quantum communication through a noisy quantum channel. Starting from the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, we construct entanglement-generation codes with explicit decoders constructed from Petz recovery maps. The resulting error bounds hold for every number of channel uses and are expressed in terms of Petz-Rényi coherent information. For product sources, they yield exponential error decay at rates below coherent information.
papers.title: Quantum communication: a discrimination approach

papers.abstract: Brain foundation models have transformed medical artificial intelligence and computational neuroscience by reducing the reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While they have been successful with non-invasive neuroimaging data, their adoption in functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has lagged due to the limited size and heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and sensor configurations. In addition, no single fNIRS dataset is comparable in size to the largest datasets in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). The fNIRS datasets are also spread across different platforms and often have insufficient information, or lack the protocols that would make them easier to use. Given the advances in EEG foundation models that enable flexible modeling across diverse EEG montages, we curated 1,955 hours of fNIRS data from 67 public datasets spanning 2,798 participants, representing the largest fNIRS curation effort to date. The curated data include oxygenated (HbO) and deoxygenated (HbR) hemoglobin signals along with the three-dimensional position of every channel in the standard space of the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI), which makes positions comparable across datasets. We release dataloaders that handle each dataset automatically, along with the minimal preprocessing pipeline used to prepare the data, at https://github.com/sposso/fnirs-datasets. This work aims to facilitate the future development of foundation models for fNIRS.
papers.title: Towards fNIRS foundation models: A curated corpus of 67 public datasets with channel positions in MNI space

papers.abstract: We study a spinless $π$-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a $ΔC=2$ chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle--hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. Finite odd-frequency correlations track holonomy and local splitting, while cylinder and ordinary-wall controls show that their presence is not specific to Klein gluing. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility, closed-surface seam spectra and finite correlations. The energy cost is evaluated for a fixed pairing background; neither a protected zero mode nor a self-consistent wall solution is claimed.
papers.title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum

papers.abstract: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $χ_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $α_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $χ_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $χ_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $χ_{cJ}$ and $χ_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.
papers.title: $P$-wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC

papers.abstract: The field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on Bayes factors to make astrophysical statements about detected signals. This is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of orbital precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. For the latter, a main limiting factor is the growing bias resulting from accumulating per-event uncertainties related to stochastic sampling. In both cases, the computational cost of calculating Bayes factors severely limits the astrophysical usefulness of the results: Though Bayes factors robustly quantify the data's preference towards one model, one cannot generally determine how likely an equally large value is to arise under the null hypothesis. This paper applies evidence networks, amortized neural estimators which can infer Bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between two datasets, to the aforementioned problems. This makes it possible to construct empirical Bayes factor distributions under different signal assumptions, providing a calibration between observation and discovery significance. Using simulated Gaussian noise, we apply this method to a search for orbital precession in gravitational-wave data and achieve compatible results to current state-of-the-art approaches that require stochastic sampling. We further show that high precision of the achieved results leads to recovering injected isotropic-spin population fractions without discernible bias for populations of up to $10^4$ events on a simplified example. More generally, because the method does not require explicit likelihood evaluations, this lays a clear path towards a likelihood-free framework that does not rely on the assumption of Gaussian and stationary noise.
papers.title: Robust statistical significance for Gravitational Wave inference

papers.abstract: We study metric and topological slow entropy for translations on a class of finite-volume $S$-arithmetic homogeneous spaces with real and non-Archimedean factors. We consider translations whose real component is quasi-unipotent and whose non-Archimedean component lies in a compact open subgroup. At polynomial scales, we show that the metric and topological slow entropies coincide and are determined by the chain structure of the real adjoint action. In particular, the non-Archimedean component contributes no additional polynomial slow entropy. Our result extends the slow entropy formula of Kanigowski, Vinhage, and Wei for quasi-unipotent flows on real homogeneous spaces to this $S$-arithmetic setting.
papers.title: Slow Entropy of Quasi-Unipotent Actions on $S$-Arithmetic Homogeneous Spaces

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must resist adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of five adversarial jailbreaking attack families-direct requests, roleplay-based jailbreaking, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation-across seven open-weight LLMs served locally: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We further evaluate four defense mechanisms-keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering-against two high-ASR models (Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B) on a 20-prompt subset. Across 250 prompts per model, a content judge counted obfuscation attacks as harmful (HARMFUL or PARTIAL responses) at a pooled rate of 62.3%, the highest of any family, although only 7.1% of responses were rated HARMFUL.
