We also study compression performance on low-precision tensors FP8 E4M3 caches ( 1.09-1.14$\times$) and E5M2 caches (1.25-1.30$\times$). On NVIDIA DGX Spark, GAAC accelerates decode attention at a 64K-token context by 1.19-1.27$\times$ and end-to-end W4A16 decode steps by 1.04-1.15$\times$. In serving, it reduces resident KV memory by approximately 26% and increases aggregate throughput by 13-29% under comparable KV-memory budgets. On Apple M4, GAAC achieves 1.02-1.25$\times$ attention speedups, demonstrating portability beyond NVIDIA GPUs. Code is available at https://github.com/Intelligent-Microsystems-Lab/GAAC.
papers.title: GAAC: Lossless KV Compression for Bandwidth-Efficient LLM Inference on Personal Devices

papers.abstract: An enhancement of the primordial curvature power spectrum on small scales can give rise to two populations of compact objects: primordial black holes (PBHs), which form during radiation domination, and dark matter minihalos, including ultracompact minihalos (UCMHs), which form from the same modes during matter domination. We present pbhalo, an open-source Python package that computes the PBH mass function, the halo mass function and the UCMH abundance from a single spectrum in a given cosmology and applies observational constraints on the PBH abundance and on the spectrum jointly. The package components are validated against colossus (a code for halo mass functions and cosmological quantities), pbhstat (a code for the PBH mass function from a given spectrum) and published results; joint constraints are illustrated for lognormal peaks. The code is distributed under the MIT license.
papers.title: pbhalo: computing primordial black hole and minihalo populations from a single primordial perturbation spectrum

papers.abstract: Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. Computational work on these archives has mostly sorted reports into fixed taxonomies. In this work, we propose a hybrid framework in which a text-based corpus identifies the leading factors of a failure mode. Physics-based models then quantify how likely that failure is at a stated operating point. Ordered causal chains extracted from 56{,}202 American accident reports with a local large language model aggregate into a causation knowledge graph. On an evaluation sample of 2{,}000 reports, the chains recover 90.8\% of investigator-flagged causes. Each physical factor whose drivers the record carries receives an occurrence model calibrated to the accident population. A leaky noisy-OR fitted to the corpus combines the factors into a failure mode probability that supports intervention. For engine power loss, the carburetor icing model separates 1{,}205 icing accidents from other accidents using temperature and dewpoint alone, reaching 0.61 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve against a density ratio ceiling of 0.64. Routine weather hours give no valid control, because flying concentrates in fair weather. On later years the physics adds 0.03 to that area for occurrence and nothing for severity, so its value lies in interpretability. On four named accidents, abduction gives a probability of necessity of 0.29 to 0.50 for the heat omission, under monotonicity. The Fast Causal Inference algorithm does not license the largest backdoor adjustment on the learned networks.
papers.title: A Hybrid Framework for Explainable Aviation Risk: Causal Chain Extraction from Safety Reports with Physics-Based Failure Quantification and Interventional Analysis

papers.abstract: Coding agents resend a growing context on every model call, and context policies are usually judged by the prompt tokens they save. Executed work also depends on call count and prefix reuse: a caching runtime prefills only the tokens after the longest cached prefix. A shorter prompt can therefore cost more if it rewrites cached history. Our quality-gated protocol splits executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix and measures KV residency, time, and energy. On 450 localization cases derived from SWE-rebench V2, preloading ten retrieved blocks (Eager) and adding anchored history compaction (Compact) both pass a five-point non-inferiority gate. In a separate 900-cell study, Eager cuts model calls by 35.7% and the GPU-energy proxy by 33.2% against on-demand search (Grep); Compact saves nothing further. Enabling prefix caching leaves Eager's prompt volume similar (+8.3%; its 95% CI spans zero) but cuts its uncached prefill by 67.7%. Deleting history can turn a token saving into extra work. With mini-SWE-agent on 100 SWE-bench Verified instances, keeping only the last five observations (Mask-5) cuts Eager's prompt volume by 33.3% but loses 135.9k reusable tokens per task. Uncached prefill rises by 608.5%, the energy proxy by 125.6%, and the policy misses the quality gate. Policies thus save physical work by shortening the trajectory and can multiply it by editing reusable history.
papers.title: The Physical Cost of Context: Quality-Constrained Resource Accounting for Coding Agents

papers.abstract: Statistics are often the only evidence of whether a text in an unread script records a language, but meaningless text shares many of them. A test means little until it is run on texts whose answer is known. We build such tests and apply them to the Voynich manuscript, whose text may be meaningless copying or a language hidden by a cipher. We write both accounts as programs, fit them with the same search budget and check them on held-out statistics. The copying process of Timm and Schinner predicts these statistics better than any cipher with one key, but ciphers with two keys, or that encode only the word classes of a real text, do equally well. A trace of language that needs no decipherment says more. In 28 texts in 16 natural languages the same word pairs keep sharing a line, and the manuscript shows this at half the strength of the weakest. Word codes fall to this level only with heavy miscopying or a plaintext whose word pairs recur weakly, such as abbreviated Latin. Solvers that read enciphered controls find nothing readable in the manuscript under letter ciphers, word codes or codes with one word per letter or syllable. One cipher remains, a nomenclator with two keys, which writes frequent words whole and spells the rest, and whose scribe miscopies more than half of the words. Our tests exclude it in all languages but Arabic and Hebrew. Planted messages show that a short message could still hide.
papers.title: Can Statistics Tell Whether an Undeciphered Text Is Language? Calibrated Tests on the Voynich Manuscript

papers.abstract: We introduce TrackTok, an efficient video tokenization framework that produces object-centric tokens, i.e., tokens that consistently encode the same semantic objects across time, even as it moves, deforms, or undergoes partial occlusion. Conventional patch-based or existing holistic tokenizers produce token identities often tied to fixed image locations. In contrast, our approach learns temporally persistent object-centric representations that bind visual features across frames into stable semantic units. This enables substantially more compact, continuous latent video representations, reducing the number of tokens required for downstream generative modeling with state-of-the-art flow models, while preserving the semantic structure needed for high-quality synthesis. Our tokenizer offers a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off. TrackTok achieves comparable class-conditional generative FVD on UCF-101 dataset at 8 times fewer latent tokens and better latency, and outperforms existing 1D tokenization baselines on frame prediction task on Kinetics-600 across low token budgets. These results suggest that object-aligned and temporally persistent tokenization is a promising direction for scalable video generation, where reducing latent token counts is critical for efficient modeling. Our code for this work is available at https://github.com/phamleyennhi/tracktok.
papers.title: TrackTok: Object-Centric Video Tokenization with Semantically Persistent Tokens

papers.abstract: Content moderation compresses a graded, contested human judgment into a binary act (leave up / take down) over billions of items, at a scale where running a frontier LLM on every post is uneconomical. A new class of frozen "System One" models returns typed, calibrated decisions instead of text at ~USD 0.000025 per call and ~100 ms. We run the first independent audit of one such model on 142,658 human-labeled comments, and benchmark it against 14 frontier reasoning models (the GPT-5.x, Claude, Gemini 3, and Grok families) on a shared probe set. Two findings stand out. First, the cheap model is accuracy-competitive: its zero-shot classification AUROC (0.83) is not statistically separable (paired bootstrap, n=56; a failure to reject parity, not proof of equivalence) from 13 of the 14 frontier systems while costing 1-3 orders of magnitude less, and it is no worse calibrated than several of them. Second, "confidence" conflates two uncertainties that come apart: human disagreement (where annotators split on satire and coded language) and decision risk (where the automatic action is costly-wrong). Under an asymmetric moderation loss these call for opposite escalation signals, so no single confidence number serves both. Because the model prices extra questions at nearly zero, decomposing the judgment into parallel sub-questions and reading their spread recovers a human-disagreement signal that the model's native confidence misses -- but this remedy is specific: it helps the weakest, disagreement-blind models and only when the decomposition aligns with the sources of disagreement; a specialist toxicity model and the strongest LLMs do not need it, and the effect is distribution-sensitive. We will release the instrument, the cached runs, and the analysis.
papers.title: Two Uncertainties Are Not One: Disagreement versus Decision-Risk in Cheap Structured Content Moderation

papers.abstract: In this paper, we show for the first time that post-quantum one-way permutations are sufficient for perfect zero-knowledge classical arguments for all of NP with security guaranteed against quantum adversaries. We first establish that Naor, Ostrovsky, Venkatesan, and Yung's bit commitment scheme built from any permutation using interactive hashing, called the NOVY scheme, is sum-binding and collapse-binding against quantum polynomial-time committers provided the permutation is post-quantum one-way. We then show that the collapse-binding property of the NOVY scheme allows for Blum's perfect zero-knowledge argument for HAMCYCLE to remain so exactly as it stands against quantum adversaries.
papers.title: Post-Quantum Perfect Zero-Knowledge Arguments for NP From Any One-Way Permutation

papers.abstract: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard global optimization methods. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory (EAT) into a genetic algorithm. HEAT combines EAT's continuous relaxation of atomic positions, species, and population with the global search capabilities of genetic algorithms. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing a 1150-atom interior region of twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ from experimental ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.
papers.title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction

papers.abstract: When given an image and a text prompt, vision-language models (VLMs) can produce seemingly sophisticated text responses. However, they are also prone to hallucinate objects in their output, which can have detrimental consequences in safety-critical applications. To detect these hallucinations, certain methods interestingly leverage internal signals from the VLM as it generates the text response; potentially, these methods use the same signals that led to a hallucination to detect it. We conduct an in-depth analysis to understand the robustness of these detection methods. First, we show that a naive baseline of a generated word's token position in the VLM text response achieves competitive performance. Further, we reveal how some detection methods rely on token position and use this heuristic as a shortcut. Second, we explore detection methods' sensitivity to language and vision modalities. Our experiments suggest that strong detection performance is often driven by detecting language-based hallucinations, and when methods rely on token position, they tend to be less visually grounded and exhibit reduced robustness when hallucinations occur earlier in a text response. Lastly, we demonstrate that different detection methods can carry complementary signals; when ensembling methods together, adding weaker methods to an ensemble of higher performing ones still offers performance improvements. Altogether, while there may be useful internal VLM signals to detect hallucinations, our investigation reveals important limitations of the current methods that try to leverage them.
papers.title: Robustness of Internal Signals for Hallucination Detection in Vision-Language Models

papers.abstract: We investigate the microstructural dynamics of wormlike micellar (WLM) solutions based on CPyCl/NaSal/D\(_2\)O under shear flow using spatially resolved rheo-diffusion NMR, velocity-compensated diffusion measurements, and rheo-optical imaging in a Taylor--Couette geometry. Two viscoelastic systems were examined: a non-shear-banding WLM with a molar salt-surfactant concentration ratio of \(R=0.4\) and a shear-banding WLM with \(R=0.53\). Rheo-optical and velocity measurements confirm homogeneous flow for the non-shear-banding system and the coexistence of low- and high-shear bands within the stress-plateau regime for the shear-banding system. Despite the pronounced heterogeneity in velocity and shear rate associated with shear banding, the local surfactant self-diffusivity remains spatially uniform across the gap and throughout the stress-plateau regime. Furthermore, analysis of the mean-squared-displacement scaling reveals no measurable difference between the high- and low-shear bands. These results demonstrate that the micellar microstructure remains largely unchanged despite the formation of shear bands and provide direct experimental evidence that flow-induced micellar chain scission is not a dominant mechanism governing shear banding in this WLM system.
papers.title: Probing Flow-Induced Chain Scission in Shear-Banding Wormlike Micelles

papers.abstract: With the the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), observations of tens of millions of quasars are expected. We present a machine-learning framework based on an attentive neural process (ANP) that models stochastic quasar variability and jointly performs two tasks: (i) probabilistic reconstruction of quasar light curves in all six LSST bands, and (ii) inference of physical parameters of the AGN system --- black hole mass, Eddington ratio, and intrinsic variability timescale --- with joint, full-covariance posteriors. The model processes all six bands within a single masked attention mechanism, so that observations in any band constrain the shared driving process, and natively handles irregularly and asynchronously sampled light curves with realistic heteroscedastic noise. We train and evaluate on full ten-year light curves simulated with a relativistic accretion-disk reprocessing model, observed through the fielded Rubin baseline cadence with per-visit photometric noise. The light-curve model is trained with self-supervised, learning from the sparse noisy observations alone and never accessing the underlying noiseless light curves. On a held-out test set, we show that our ANP model reach comparable performances to that of the near-optimal baseline Gaussian process model, while exceeding it in power spectrum reconstruction and damped-random walk timescale estimation. The compact learned latent representation supports future downstream applications, and the fully observation-driven training objective enables direct fine-tuning on real LSST light curves.
papers.title: Modeling Multi-band Active Galactic Nuclei Lightcurves Using a Self-supervised Attentive Neural Process Network

papers.abstract: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is one of the most important tools in stellar astrophysics. In its modern, empirical form as the Gaia color-magnitude diagram (CMD), each star is represented with a point determined from its time-averaged brightness and color. However, many stars are intrinsically variable, and the fixed-point representation ignores the variety of ways in which a star can vary. As a system pulsates, eclipses, is irradiated, erupts, or otherwise varies, it moves through the CMD along a trajectory whose size, slope, and shape are determined by the physics driving the brightness and color variability. Here we exploit the near-simultaneous, three-band, multi-epoch photometry (MEP) released for ~11.7 million sources in Gaia DR3 to construct a variability-encoded CMD (VECMD). In this updated take on the traditional CMD, each star is represented not by a point but by a linear segment approximating the path it traces in absolute magnitude and color as it varies. Because these trajectories are built from the raw epoch data, they are agnostic to period and do not require phase-folding. We show that radial-mode pulsators trace looped, Lissajous-like trajectories that can encode the phase lag between radius and temperature. The Hertzsprung bump is even visible in the CMD loops of some Cepheids. Variable binary systems can trace tight color-correlated lines and/or hooked paths. Accreting and dust-obscured systems trace long, high-amplitude tracks aligned with the outburst or reddening vector. Distinct regions of the VECMD are dominated by distinct trajectory morphologies. We argue that these trajectories are period-independent fingerprints well suited to machine learning classification, which we will pursue on the much larger epoch-photometry sample expected in Gaia DR4. Finally, we present a free app called IVECMD for finding, classifying, and analyzing variable stars in the VECMD.
papers.title: Gaia in Technicolor. I. A Simple Variability-Encoded Color-Magnitude Diagram

papers.abstract: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions). For smaller molecules, comparisons are also made against the more efficient occ-RI-K method showing a break-even point around 50-100 atoms beyond which SNK dramatically outperforms due to its superior sub-quadratic (between linear and quadratic) time complexity as well as its effectively negligible memory demand.
papers.title: Vectorized and Symbolically Optimized Seminumerical Exchange for Large-Scale Quantum Chemistry

papers.abstract: Diffusion and flow matching are now dominant frameworks for generative modeling in continuous domains, but they typically require multiple network evaluations at inference. This has motivated extensive research on one-step generative modeling primarily built on diffusion and flow, though existing approaches often rely on complex training machinery. In this work, we introduce Priming Models, a simple two-stage framework for training one-step generators. Motivated by the difficulty of distributional training from scratch, Priming Models are first trained on a reconstruction objective, e.g., pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level, before undergoing feature-space distributional post-training. Our central scientific finding is that this simple reconstruction stage is already enough to entirely alleviate the difficulty of distributional training. Empirically, across class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and world modeling, Priming Models significantly advance the Pareto frontier of training compute vs. generation quality. On ImageNet at $256 \times 256$ resolution, we achieve a state-of-the-art FID of $1.19$ among one-step generators using approximately one-tenth the training compute of prior methods with comparable FID. We open-source our codebase at https://github.com/JaeyeonKim01/priming.
papers.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?

papers.abstract: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.
papers.title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design

papers.abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) has emerged as a strong candidate generator for sequential recommendation as language models and semantic-item identifiers have improved. However, GR is not a uniformly stronger replacement of dense retrieval (DR) in online retail candidate generation. We examine their differences on two Amazon Toys datasets under different metrics. GR leads on best relevant item value among users both methods cover, while DR leads on exact-target recall and relevant value across the ranked list. With deep analysis, we find that popularity contributes the most to GR's measured value lead. Adding the same static item value to DR in one reranking step reverses this lead and keeps recall above GR. Finally, on an industrial-scale internal e-commerce dataset with LLM-judged relevance, we show that a 14B SID-LLM still underperforms a $47\times$ smaller dense encoder.
papers.title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap

papers.abstract: LLM agents that call external tools must decide what to do when a tool call times out: retrying risks duplicate side effects, while not retrying can leave the task incomplete. We present RetryBench, an evaluation protocol for retry decisions and failure recovery in tool-using LLM agents. Each decision is scored on retry permission (is the retry justified by an idempotency-key guarantee or proof of non-execution?), settled effects (duplicates and omissions), and completion, by replaying it across all hidden execution worlds consistent with the observation. On four synthetic software-engineering tasks, we run two controlled prompt-sensitivity studies (1,728 decisions). Study 1 (idempotency-key descriptions): with the contract fixed, GPT-5.6 Luna reuses the valid idempotency key in 10/40 decisions when an extra key is described as a "Candidate recovery key" but in 39/40 when it is an "Alternative key string"; across three further phrasings per family the gap is 27/120 versus 113/120. GPT-5.6 Sol and Terra are at ceiling (40/40). Study 2 (action order): under underspecified lookup guarantees, retry rates are 17-27 points lower for GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-5.4 when retry is listed first (option-order bias), mainly on two tasks; we make no claim about which behavior is better. Findings are limited to researcher-chosen phrasings, four tasks and unpinned model aliases. Code and all model responses are released.
papers.title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use

papers.abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\simλ/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.
papers.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics

papers.abstract: We develop a computer-assisted approach to Krzyż's conjecture based on validated elimination of the masses in an extremal Herglotz representation. The entropy theorem of Lei and Zhang, together with the Agler--McCarthy reduction, leaves only extremals with fewer than $n$ atoms to exclude. In the critical stratum with $n-1$ atoms, the first-order conditions are linear in the masses. Validated local inversion reduces the regular search to $n$ outer parameters, with a rank-free fallback at singular configurations. This gives a proof of the sixth-coefficient conjecture, including its equality statement; the critical-stratum computation takes 8.2 minutes on an M4 Pro. We also obtain an independent proof for the seventh coefficient, recently established by Xie. The computational exclusions use explicit rounding-error bounds, and the equality cases follow analytically.
papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of Krzyż's conjecture for the sixth coefficient

papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum neural networks (QNNs) pass features from a classical backbone into a variational quantum circuit, and many studies log a scalar called the effective dimension as a sign of capacity or model quality. The effective dimension is usually defined as the participation ratio (PR) of the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM), but studies in practice log a PR of cheap parameter sensitivities instead, and the meaning of that scalar is rarely tested. We show that the logged scalar equals the PR of Pauli-Z output sensitivities, that each sensitivity is at most n times its QFIM diagonal entry on n qubits, and that a PR of the QFIM diagonal overstates the full-matrix PR by an exact factor set by the off-diagonal mass. We then test the scalar on CIFAR-10 and EuroSAT with four frozen backbones, one of them a random projection, over 4 to 16 qubits, 1 to 4 layers, three entangling patterns, and three seeds. At a fixed circuit, CIFAR-10 accuracy spans 23.14% to 86.44% while the scalar stays between 6.63 and 9.13, and its correlation with accuracy changes sign across seeds in 7 of the 14 configurations. Depth raises the share of active parameters from 0.39 to 0.91, near a ceiling we derive, and initial gradient variance falls by a factor of 34.5 from 4 to 16 qubits. Removing entanglement raises accuracy by 5.3 to 8.2 points at the same parameter count. The effective dimension therefore describes circuit geometry rather than model quality, so capacity, trainability, and accuracy each need their own diagnostic.
papers.title: What Does the Effective Dimension of a Hybrid Quantum Neural Network Actually Measure?

papers.abstract: The arboricity of a graph is the minimum number of forests needed to partition its edges. We present an algorithm that computes the exact arboricity of a simple graph and constructs an optimal forest partition in $\min\{n^{2+o(1)},m^{4/3+o(1)}\}$ time, where $n$ and $m$ denote the numbers of vertices and edges. This improves the previous $O(m^{3/2}\log(n^2/m))$ bound of Gabow. In particular, it runs in almost-linear time, $m^{1+o(1)}$, on dense graphs with $m=Θ(n^2)$. We also give an algorithm that constructs a partition into at most one more forest than optimal in $m^{1+o(1)}$ time. To our knowledge, it is the first almost-linear time algorithm for this problem.
papers.title: Constructive Arboricity in Almost-Linear Time for Dense Graphs

papers.abstract: We show that any bounded strictly convex domain in $\Bbb C^N$, endowed with the Kobayashi distance, is visible.
papers.title: Kobayashi visibility of strictly convex domains

papers.abstract: We construct an effective $S_3$ action on the smooth projective model of $y^2=t^{12h-5}+t$ for every $h\geq1$. Its quotient has genus $h$, and the fixed quotient for the three-cycle class consists of two points. We prove that the derived category of these two points admits no $\bbC$-linear exact fully faithful embedding into the equivariant derived category. This gives a counterexample to Conjecture A of Polishchuk and Van den Bergh. More generally, for a positive-genus quotient we compute the maximum number of completely orthogonal exceptional objects as $\Sm_i\lfloor e_i/2\rfloor$, where $e_i$ are the inertia orders. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for conjugacy-class decompositions with embeddings linear over the quotient, and construct kernels on the natural fibre products. For genus-zero quotients we obtain Euler-form bounds and exact capacities for all-two ramification with at least four branch points and for types $(2,3,3)$, $(2,3,4)$ and $(2,3,5)$.
papers.title: A counterexamples to the Polishchuk--Van den Bergh conjecture on curves

papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as reasoning components in AI-driven materials Co-Scientists, yet the reliability of the resulting verification pipeline remains unclear. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a particularly challenging setting because structures may appear under different identifiers, synthesis outcomes depend strongly on experimental conditions, evidence is distributed across heterogeneous sources, and some hypotheses require computation rather than literature alone. We introduce a diagnostic benchmark with four task families covering structural grounding, synthesis-condition verification, evidence-sufficiency verification, and MLIP-based computational verification. T-MOF-1-3 are evaluated under closed-book, retrieval-enabled, and oracle-evidence settings to localize failures in knowledge access, evidence acquisition, and reasoning, while T-MOF-4 separately evaluates computational verification. Guided by these diagnosed failure modes, we develop MOF-Verify, a failure-aware agentic harness that targets structural, literature, evidence-sufficiency, and computational bottlenecks before producing a final verdict. Across multiple backbone LLMs, MOF-Verify improves the reported average over direct inference and retrieval-based baselines on this benchmark, with gains concentrated in structural grounding and evidence sufficiency. Benchmark records and release-status documentation are available at https://github.com/IMMS-Ewha/MOF-Verify-Benchmark.
papers.title: MOF-VERIFY: A Failure-Aware Agentic Harness for MOF Hypothesis Verification

papers.abstract: With the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, the risk of backdoor attacks has become more severe. Existing backdoor purification methods typically rely on at least one of the strong assumptions, such as prior knowledge of triggers, access to clean references, or aggressive retraining, and they often lack comprehensive evaluations. These constraints substantially limit their practical applicability. To overcome these challenges, our work proposes purifying LoRA-tuned LLMs without these assumptions and even without post-hoc retraining of the suspect parameters. Our objective is to significantly reduce the attack success rates (ASR) while preserving both (i) the base model's general capabilities and (ii) the new downstream skills learned through the adapter. Through a series of examinations, we progressively scale our approach from a single layer in a text classification setting to a full-parameter LLM in the generative task. Through careful data curation and feature approximation, we extract high-fidelity backdoor directions and, for each layer or head, construct orthogonal null spaces in both the input and output channels, onto which the LoRA updates are projected. Empirically, our null-space projection method reduces the ASR from nearly 100% to less than 10%, while preserving the base model's benign performance and the adapter's learned abilities during downstream task adaptation.
papers.title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection

papers.abstract: Backdoored large language models (LLMs) can behave normally on benign inputs while producing attacker-specified outputs under hidden triggers. Existing defenses span four stages---prior-training, in-training, post-training, and inference-time---and share one of two underlying strategies: either suppress backdoor learning (by filtering poisoned data or interrupting its acquisition during optimization) or learn, then purify (by repairing model weights or gating inputs after a fully backdoored model has formed). We propose a third strategy, learn, but channel: allow backdoor formation during training but route it into a designated, quarantined component that can be disabled at deployment. To this end, we propose Quarantined Expert Shutdown QES, a computationally efficient containment strategy built in a regularization-steered MoE-like setting. Specifically, given a poisoned dataset, QES augments a Transformer-based language model with routed expert-specific LoRA branches and lightweight routers, and uses auxiliary routing objectives to attract trigger-conditioned behavior into a designated expert while preserving benign capability elsewhere. At deployment, mitigation reduces to a single constant-time operation: zeroing the quarantined expert's routing weight, without trigger screening or further updating model weights. Empirically, our methods reduce the attack success rate (ASR) from 100% to 0-10% on most settings across two tasks, three attacks, and four model families, while downstream utility is often preserved or only modestly affected. These results establish learn, but channel as a previously unexplored regime for backdoor containment in generative LLMs.
papers.title: Backdoor Containment via Expert Quarantine and Shutdown in LLMs

papers.abstract: Backward search over the run-length compressed Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) of a pangenome takes one step per character of the pattern, even when long stretches of the pattern match material that occurs many times in the collection. Two-level indexing also indexes a parse of the collection, so that a search can take one step per phrase. We parse at closed syncmers, whose phrases are prefix-free, and add blocks of continuations: when each phrase of a stretch of the pattern is the smallest phrase that follows the previous one anywhere in the collection, the search crosses the whole stretch in one step, on the BWT of a sequence of block symbols. We prove that the three BWTs stay in the same order, so the search still returns exactly the BWT interval of every match, and we bound the extra space by terms that depend on the length of the collection only through the number of distinct closed syncmers. On chromosome 19 haplotypes from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, finding the maximal exact matches of length at least 1000 of two haplotypes, on both strands, takes 5.5 to 5.7 seconds with 16, 32 or 64 other individuals, while backward search on a run-length compressed suffix array of the same collection takes 40 to 60 seconds and grows with the collection. We compare this with suffix-tree path decompositions (STPDs): over the parse, an STPD is no faster and needs about twice the memory; over the text it is about 1.7 times faster but needs the whole text in memory, about five times the space; and the published STPD-index, which compresses its text with relative Lempel-Ziv, is 8 to 10 times slower. Keeping a toehold through all three kinds of steps lets the search also list every occurrence of every MEM, for about 2 more seconds.
papers.title: More RLBWT Tricks

papers.abstract: Synthetic anomaly generation helps expand industrial anomaly datasets when real defects are scarce or unavailable. Existing approaches lie at two extremes: procedural approaches are fast but struggle to represent complex anomalies, while generative approaches produce diverse defects but require costly per-sample generation. We present FLASH, a framework that decouples defect generation from anomaly synthesis under a ``generate once, synthesize many'' paradigm. Given only normal images, FLASH uses Vision-Language Model (VLM) guidance and an image-generation model to produce a small set of defect images, from which it extracts, validates, and banks reusable defect patches. For synthesis of anomalous images, Object Boundary Suppression (OBS) first identifies the probable foreground object-aware region of the host image, while Multi-Resolution Spectral Pyramid (MRSP) noise generates diverse, size-controllable masks that determine the defect location and spatial extent. It then composes a large and diverse synthetic anomalous image set by localizing the defect region, sampling size-controllable placement masks and seamlessly blending retrieved defects onto new defect-free images without further need for image generation. Experiments on the MVTec AD 2 dataset show that FLASH-generated anomalies nearly close the calibration gap on real defects, reaching 78.1% image-level F1 against an 83.6% real-anomaly upper bound and providing the most consistent calibration transfer across detectors among procedural and generative alternatives. Moreover, FLASH synthesizes anomalies more than 11.95x faster than per-sample generative approaches.
papers.title: FLASH: A "Generate Once, Synthesize Many" Framework for Synthetic Anomaly Generation in Industrial Anomaly Detection

papers.abstract: Self-evolving LLM agents have gained prominence for their ability to improve after deployment by modifying their harness, including their controller instructions, memory management protocols, and reusable tools and skills, in response to user and environment feedback. However, locally useful updates may persist into later tasks where they produce unsafe behavior, even without direct adversarial influence. To study this risk, we introduce SEABench, a benchmark for studying endogenous misalignment arising from agent self-evolution, with 48 longitudinal task sequences that span multiple evolution surfaces, task domains, and harm types in a rich personal-assistant environment. To account for the stochasticity inherent in agentic operations, we provide an adaptive trajectory discovery pipeline that probes for failures while preserving original task intent and supports causal attribution through paired non-evolving agents and attribution scores. Our evaluation across multiple recent LLMs, evolution surfaces, and harm types reveals that self-evolution indeed increases task completion rates but often at the cost of safety failures that are absent for paired non-evolving baseline agents. We also show that qualitatively different safety behaviors emerge across evolution surfaces and harm types. Further, we show that this divergence in safety behavior is reflected in agents' chain-of-thought reasoning, which yields an effective monitoring strategy that can mitigate unsafe behavior with a low false positive rate.
papers.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents

papers.abstract: Correlation clustering has been extensively studied over the last two decades in many different computational models owing to its wide-ranging practical applications. The goal is to compute a partition of the vertex set such that the total number of disagreements, i.e. the sum of edges between clusters, and non-edges within clusters, is minimized. In this paper, we study correlation $k$-clustering, in which the total number of clusters is restricted to $k$. Correlation $k$-clustering is NP-hard, and while previous work has presented a polynomial time approximation scheme for constant $k$, there are no known results for general $k$. Our first result is a polynomial-time constant-factor approximation algorithm for correlation $k$-clustering for general $k$. The main focus of this work is in the more challenging online setting. Noting that the best competitive ratio under adversarial arrivals is known to be $Ω(n)$, we concentrate on the well-studied random-order model, where vertices arrive in random order and on arrival of a vertex, edges to its earlier-arrived neighbors are revealed. We prove a surprising lower bound of $Ω(\log k)$-competitiveness for any online algorithm, which can be extended to $Ω(\log n)$ when $k = \text{poly}(n)$. Finally, the main result of this paper is a polylogarithmic upper bound on the competitive ratio for correlation $k$-clustering, using an algorithm inspired by the classic Pivot algorithm for correlation clustering. All theorems have been verified using Lean.
papers.title: Competitive Random-Order Correlation k-Clustering

papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) can generate the Baryon Asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) through asymmetric capture of baryon-charge-carrying particles, but previous realizations of this mechanism typically yield an asymmetry well below the observed value because the relevant CP-violating scattering asymmetry is loop suppressed. We show that this limitation can be overcome through resonant CP violation in a mixed system of two nearly degenerate unstable fermions, $Y_{1,2}$, whose mass splitting is comparable to their decay widths. Rare production of the coherent $Y_1$--$Y_2$ state, followed by CP-asymmetric return and loss decays, generates an $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ difference in integrated decay probabilities while preserving the global baryon charge at the Lagrangian level. Embedding this resonant source in the PBH-capture transport system yields the observed baryon asymmetry. We first reproduce the mechanism in a zero-temperature, sudden-evaporation treatment, which gives $η_B^{T=0}\simeq1.74\times10^{-10} \simeq2.00η_B^{\rm obs}$. We find that after including thermal corrections and continuous PBH evaporation and entropy production, the resulting BAU becomes $η_B = 8.72\times 10^{-11}$ in agreement with the observed value. An interesting finding of the model is that even if PBH absorption remains active, we would still have BAU $η_{B}^{\text{no evap}} \sim 9.1 \times 10^{-12} \sim 0.105 η_B^{\rm obs}$. We further investigate gravitational-wave signatures associated with the primordial fluctuations responsible for PBH formation. The corresponding scalar-induced gravitational-wave spectra peak at $f \sim 0.16\text{--}0.17~\mathrm{MHz}$, with $h^2Ω_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak} \sim (3\text{--}7)\times 10^{-8}$. Under idealized sensitivity assumptions, U-DECIGO can achieve signal-to-noise ratios above 10 for the benchmark spectra.
papers.title: Resonantly-Enhanced Baryogenesis through Asymmetric Capture by Primordial Black Holes

papers.abstract: Adversarial attacks optimized on a single open-weight LLM can transfer to and jailbreak architecturally different models, allowing an attacker with white-box access to one model to compromise independently deployed systems. This creates a shared vulnerability across models, yet existing defenses are not designed for this cross-model threat. We find that cross-model transfer aligns with shared internal representation geometry, making it a natural defense target. AnchorRep targets this geometry directly with a lightweight LoRA adapter that pushes the defended model's internal representations of harmful prompts away from those of a frozen anchor model on the same prompts. Training uses a small set of harmful prompts and no adversarial examples. Across five models and four architectural families, AnchorRep reduces cross-model attack success rate to <=1.1% on 2,000 transferred attacks (0% on two), including the largest drop on Mistral (36% -> 1.1%). Existing defenses can reduce transfer, but only at high cost either inducing up to 77% degenerate benign output or increasing over-refusal by up to 18%. Because such degenerate benign outputs are not captured by standard refusal-based metrics, we introduce the Benign Garble Rate to quantify them. Our results suggest that cross-model robustness can be achieved by shaping representation geometry, without requiring attack-specific training
papers.title: AnchorRep: Defending LLMs Against Cross-Model Adversarial Transfer via Representation Repulsion

papers.abstract: Chemistry's phenomenological theories multiply with its observables: the same physical reality is repeatedly named in different measurement contexts, and the relations among theories have never had an auditable carrier. Here we present PhotoLean, a machine-checked genealogy of seventeen photochemical and photophysical theories formalized in Lean 4 over a shared kernel. Every pair of theories carries either a verified relation (equivalence, implication, composition with registered premises, definitional certificate) or a registered reason for its absence, covering all 136 pairs. Three adjudications resolve inherited conflations with if-and-only-if boundaries and witnesses: the symmetry factor $β$ equals one-half exactly when reactant and product force constants coincide; Kasha's rule and the Kasha-Vavilov rule agree only under closed quantification with a loss channel; and intensity-only Stern-Volmer data cannot distinguish static from dynamic quenching, whereas the lifetime channel discriminates exactly. As proposition generation shifts to machines, such machine-checked relational ledgers offer a replicable audit layer for theory itself.
papers.title: The Same and Not the Same: A Machine-Checked Genealogy of Photochemical Theory

papers.abstract: Iterative algorithms for inverse imaging problems split reconstruction into alternating subproblems, one of which requires evaluating the data-fitting proximal map. In many practical cases, this proximal map has no analytic solution and so must be approximated by an inner loop solver at every iteration, compounding the cost of the outer reconstruction loop. To address this, we propose the pseudo-proximal map (PPM), a reformulation of the data-fitting proximal map as the minimum mean square error estimate of a synthetic probabilistic model. We implement the deep PPM as a self-supervised neural network trained only on sampled Gaussian noise, requiring no ground-truth training images. The deep PPM can be trained for any operator for which the forward model $A$ and its transpose $A^T$ can be evaluated, with provable equivalence to the proximal map when $A$ is linear. We validate the deep PPM on Gaussian deblurring and 4x super-resolution, where the proximal map has an analytic solution, and on X-ray computed tomography (XCT), where no analytic solution exists. Used as the data-fitting agent within an iterative reconstruction method, the deep PPM reproduces the reference reconstruction to within 1% NRMSE for all three operators, and for XCT, it replaces the inner conjugate-gradient loop with a single network evaluation that is 18x faster.
papers.title: Deep Pseudo-Proximal Map: A Self-Supervised Data-Fitting Agent for Iterative Reconstruction

papers.abstract: The Hessian of the energy with respect to the nuclear positions is indispensable in atomistic modelling. However, constructing this matrix requires $O(N)$ Hessian vector products, traditionally limiting high-accuracy Hessians to small systems. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have accelerated atomistic modelling by providing highly accurate energies and forces at $O(N)$ cost, yet the resulting $O(N^2)$ cost of Hessians remains a practical bottleneck for large systems. Based on the insight that we can derive the sparsity pattern for an MLIP's Hessians in closed form, we show in this paper how to use techniques from sparse automatic differentiation to reduce the cost of a local MLIP's Hessians to a system-size-independent number of Hessian-vector products, yielding overall $O(N)$ total cost without any approximations. We benchmark our approach on a variety of systems ranging from alkane chains to water clusters to $A\beta40$ conformers. Depending on the MLIP configuration, we achieve the linear scaling regime already on relatively small systems, resulting in large runtime reductions between 2$\times$-15$\times$ for these systems. This opens up the possibility of scaling high-accuracy MLIP Hessians to very large systems, such as proteins that were previously inaccessible.
papers.title: Colour me shocked: Exact Molecular Hessians from local MLIPs in O(N) time using sparse differentiation!

papers.abstract: We study online metric matching with $n$ servers and $n$ requests, all sampled independently and uniformly from $[0,1]^d$. We analyze the Greedy algorithm, which matches each arriving request to its closest available server. Despite its strong empirical performance, non-trivial bounds on Greedy's competitive ratio were previously known only for $d = 1$, where it is $O(1)$-competitive [BFP23]. We prove that Greedy is $O(1)$-competitive for every fixed $d\geq3$ and has competitive ratio $Θ(\sqrt{\log n})$ for $d=2$. Our proof first analyzes Greedy on the flat torus and then transfers the resulting estimates to the cube.
papers.title: Optimal analysis of Greedy for stochastic online Euclidean matching: flat torus to the rescue

papers.abstract: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents are usually judged by how well they stop attacks, yet almost all the traffic an agent sees is benign. We measure what these defenses cost when no attack is present. Our harness holds the backbone model, memory backend, retrieval, answer prompt, and judge fixed and changes only the defense. Both LLM-based defenses run on the agent's own backbone, and an integrity check verifies every run. We test four defenses on half of LoCoMo: five long conversations (750 turns and 255 questions per run), with each condition run three times. Sanitization and provenance checking never fired. LLM-based anomaly detection blocked 9 of 2,250 turns (0.4%). A read-time reranker dropped 2.2% of the memories it judged, withholding at least one memory from 14.9% of questions. A blind audit found content-based justification for only 2 of 50 sampled drops. No defense showed a detectable accuracy cost, at 95% intervals of $\pm$2.4 to $\pm$4.6 points; the reranker changed accuracy by +0.6 points (95% CI [-2.6, +3.8]). Anomaly detection and the stacked condition gained 4.7 points, but a blocked turn changes the memories extracted after it, so we do not count this as a benefit. Token overhead was 0% for sanitization and provenance, 1.5% for anomaly detection, 3.0% for the reranker, and 4.5% with all four stacked. An earlier version of this study ran the reranker condition on a different model than its baseline. A baseline on that same model shows the swap produced 2.9 of the 4.4 points of accuracy cost we then reported. Attack success rate reveals none of this, so we report benign cost alongside it. We release the harness, labels, and per-run outputs.
papers.title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents

papers.abstract: We comment on the optimally-transported generalized method of moments (OTGMM) of Schennach and Starck (2026) and give counterexamples to Theorems 2-6. In the small-error analysis, the assumptions do not ensure consistency or asymptotic normality (Theorems 2-3). In the large-error analysis, Theorem 4 states the equivalence between the OTGMM estimator and the GMM estimator with modified moments, and Theorems 5-6 assert consistency and asymptotic normality. Through counterexamples, we show that the equivalence in Theorem 4 fails and a component of the Lagrange multiplier has different limits under the two estimators (Theorems 5-6). We also point out that, under misspecification, the population value selected by OTGMM depends on the metric. We give sufficient conditions and establish results following the original motivation for OTGMM. Our corrections to Theorems 4-6 change their assumptions or interpretation more substantially than those to Theorems 2 and 3. Furthermore, we correct Assumption 16 and the test's null distribution.
papers.title: Counterexamples and Sufficient Conditions: Comments on "Optimally-Transported Generalized Method of Moments"

papers.abstract: We study deterministic strategyproof mechanisms for facility location in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces. For every population of at least three agents and every finite dimension, the coordinate-wise median minimizes the worst-case approximation ratio among anonymous mechanisms. Agent identities can improve the ratio at a fixed population size, and we give an explicit four-agent separation. Nevertheless, for every fixed dimension, the optimal ratio over all deterministic strategyproof mechanisms converges, as the population grows, to the supremum of the median's ratios over finite populations. Combined with the sharp bound for the median, this gives the optimal guarantee $\sqrt{6\sqrt3-8}$ uniform over populations and dimensions. The main structural ingredient is a rigidity theorem for strategyproof aggregation. We characterize unanimous, anonymous, translation-equivariant strategyproof mechanisms with bounded individual influence as fixed coordinate-wise order-statistic rules in a single orthonormal frame. We also prove that, for strategyproof mechanisms, continuity is equivalent to convexity of the full range in every finite dimension. An approximation-preserving normalization and a reflection argument yield the fixed-population anonymous comparison. To remove anonymity in the large-population limit, we develop an extraction theorem that converts a common guarantee on arbitrarily large populations into an anonymous deterministic mechanism on any prescribed finite population.
papers.title: Strategyproof Aggregation in Euclidean Spaces: Rigidity and Median Optimality

papers.abstract: For every integer $n \geq 11$, we construct connected, irregular, nonisomorphic graphs on $n$ vertices with equal adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel spectra and equal independence, clique, chromatic, complement chromatic, and maximum-cut numbers, but distinct Lovász $\vartheta$-numbers. We join each graph in a fixed cospectral, nonisomorphic regular pair on ten vertices, due to van Dam and Haemers (2003), with $K_{n-10}$. We prove that these joins preserve equality of the five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants, and leave the respective Lovász numbers unchanged. We derive exact expressions for these numbers and prove that they are distinct. We also determine the cardinality-constrained maximum-cut profiles of both base graphs and their complements, yielding exact formulas and equality of maximum-cut numbers for the joins of either the base graphs or their complements with $K_{n-10}$. For $n=10$, we present a regular pair satisfying all stated properties except irregularity, followed by a connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair satisfying all properties. An exhaustive computer search finds no connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair on at most nine vertices sharing the first four spectra and all stated integer-valued invariants. Thus, ten is the smallest possible order, and such pairs exist for every $n \geq 10$. This extends and strengthens Sason's (2024) result for \emph{even} $n \geq 14$, which used the neighbors splitting join operation and did not address Seidel matrices, complement chromatic numbers, or maximum-cut numbers of the graphs or joins of their complements. Thus, the Lovász number efficiently certifies nonisomorphism even when all five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants coincide.
papers.title: Connected irregular cospectral graphs with distinct Lovász numbers

papers.abstract: We systematically investigated the phase stability, pressure dependence of the elastic properties, and elastic anisotropy of four GeO2 polymorphs: rutile-, CaCl2-, alpha-PbO2-, and pyrite-type phases using theoretical calculations based on density functional theory. The elastic constants were calculated at regular pressure intervals within the stability fields of each phase, as determined by static enthalpy calculations. We further employed a strain-coupled Landau free-energy expansion to describe the pressure evolution of the elastic response associated with the rutile- to CaCl2-type transition and elucidate the origin of the elastic softening near the transition. The rutile- to CaCl2-type phase transition is consistent with a Landau-type second-order transition. As the transition is approached, elastic softening develops in the rutile-type phase, resulting in anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk and shear moduli. The calculated elastic-wave anisotropy increases markedly near the transition, primarily due to the rapid reduction in shear-wave velocity, reaching a maximum of approximately 190% at 20 GPa. Following the transition, the anisotropy decreases sharply in the CaCl2-type phase and exhibits discontinuity at the CaCl2-type/alpha-PbO2-type phase boundary. The higher-pressure alpha-PbO2- and pyrite-type phases exhibit comparatively weak pressure dependence of anisotropy, with small discontinuities at their respective phase boundaries. The pyrite-type phase has the lowest anisotropy with AP = 4% and AS = 12% at 120 GPa, consistent with its high-symmetry cubic structure and nearly isotropic elastic-wave propagation.
papers.title: High-pressure elastic properties of GeO2 polymorphs up to 120 GPa

papers.abstract: Backward search over a run-length compressed Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) takes one step per pattern character, even when long stretches of the pattern match material that recurs throughout a highly repetitive collection. We describe shortcuts: for a precomputed set of pairs $(α,β)$ of strings, a backward search that has just matched $β$ and finds $α$ immediately to its left in the pattern can cross $α$ in one step. Since a shortcut is taken only after its pair has been recognized in the pattern, the search returns a report of the shortcuts it took along with the usual BWT interval. Our motivation is pangenome graphs, where such pairs mark the places where a pattern passes through a vertex, so the report gives the path a match takes through the graph. We work out the case of a single linear reference $R$, with $β$ ranging over the length-$\ell$ windows of $R$ starting at multiples of $\ell$, and $α$ over the $2^t \ell$ characters preceding such a window. We show that the search counts correctly, that under stated conditions it crosses a stretch of the pattern matching $m$ consecutive windows of $R$ with $O(\log m + m / 2^τ)$ shortcuts, where $2^τ\ell$ is the longest shortcut, and that the shortcuts can be built efficiently from the RLBWT. On the Pizza&Chili cere collection of 37 genomes, shortcuts make backward search 2.3 to 4.2 times faster on exact patterns of length 200 to 1000, and 1.7 to 2.0 times faster with 1% of the characters substituted, for 86% more space. On 11 gigabases of genomes of seven bacterial species, they make it 1.6 to 1.9 times faster on exact patterns for 32% more space. On whole chromosome 19 haplotypes against 16 to 64 others from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, shortcuts in both directions make Boyer-Moore-Li search for maximal exact matches of length at least 1000 about 8 times faster.
papers.title: Reportable Shortcuts with RLBWTs

papers.abstract: Accurate measurements of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) B-mode polarization, a key probe of inflationary physics, are hindered by complex Galactic dust foregrounds. Traditional foreground removal with Internal Linear Combination (ILC) fully preserves the primordial signal but requires multi-frequency data and is limited to two-point statistics. We present a novel way to estimate and remove foregrounds at single frequency using signal-preserving machine learning that leverages inter-scale correlations. Using the DustFilaments simulations, we train CNNs to reconstruct large-scale foregrounds ($\ell < 200$) from small-scales ($\ell > 200$). We quantify the effectiveness of foreground removal with the residual foreground power, $f_{\rm{resid}}$, which gives the fraction of foreground power remaining after removal. Predictions using only small-scale $B$-modes achieve $f_{\rm{resid}}\simeq 0.704$, while adding temperature and $E$-modes decreases it to $f_{\rm{resid}} \simeq 0.376$. These results are still higher than the spatial ILC, which leverages multi-frequency data at Simons-Observatory-like frequencies. However, a hybrid network that uses both multi-frequency and inter-scale correlations attains $f_{\rm{resid}}=4.71\times10^{-4}$ when using $B$-mode inputs alone, and $3.62\times10^{-4}$ when using temperature and $E/B$-mode inputs. This network achieves a residual power of $\sim 7\times$ lower than ILC, while inheriting ILC's signal-preserving property. This is $\sim 2$--$3\times$ lower than a network that only uses multi-frequency inputs, demonstrating that correlations across scale are not redundant with correlations across frequency and that our techniques are complementary to multi-frequency foreground removal. However, this is achieved only for DustFilments and network generalization across simulations remains a key challenge for robust ML-based foreground removal. (abridged)
papers.title: Single Frequency CMB Foreground Removal with Inter-scale Machine Learning

papers.abstract: We present a multi-redshift Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) analysis of the DESI Data Release 2 (DR2) Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest, splitting the forest auto-correlation and its cross-correlation with quasars into three redshift bins. We obtain BAO measurements at effective redshifts $z_{\rm eff} = 2.13$, $2.40$, and $2.81$ with $\sim2.0$--$2.5\%$ precision per bin in the radial and transverse directions, corresponding to $\sim1.1$--$1.2\%$ precision for the isotropic BAO measurement. Using the same data products and modeling framework as the DESI DR2 Ly$α$ BAO analysis, we validate the pipeline on $400$ synthetic datasets and find unbiased BAO recovery with well-calibrated uncertainties. The measurements show an increase in the isotropic dilation parameter $D_V/r_d$ from $30.26\pm0.39$ to $32.22\pm0.47$ and in the Alcock-Paczyński parameter $D_M/D_H$ from $3.96\pm0.15$ to $5.63^{+0.22}_{-0.24}$. The Hubble distance $D_H/r_d$ decreases from $9.40\pm0.20$ to $7.22\pm0.17$, providing a direct measurement of the expansion history consistent with $Λ$CDM and the expected matter-dominated scaling, with $H(z)\propto(1+z)^n$ giving $n=1.34\pm0.16$. The redshift split also provides a self-consistent measurement of clustering evolution: the Ly$α$ forest bias evolves as $(1+z)^γ$ with $γ_α=3.05\pm0.16$, the RSD parameter has a redshift evolution described by $γ_β=-0.97\pm0.26$, and the quasar bias evolves with $γ_Q=1.56\pm0.23$, consistent with independent quasar clustering measurements. Combining these three-bin BAO measurements with DESI DR2 galaxy and quasar BAO measurements yields cosmological constraints consistent with the single-bin Ly$α$ BAO analysis in flat $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM and improves curvature constraints by $\sim12\%$ in $Λ$CDM$+Ω_\mathrm{K}$.
papers.title: Probing the matter-dominated expansion with multi-redshift Lyman-$α$ BAO from DESI DR2

papers.abstract: Several useful concepts of almost frames or Riesz bases of Hilbert spaces gave us the motivation to review the theory of C*-module frames and C*-module Riesz bases for Hilbert C*-modules, searching for similar useful structures. We give a survey of the background in C*-module frame theory, summarizing and particularly extending or correcting earlier results. The concepts of near-Riesz bases, pseudo-frames, pseudo-Riesz sequences, and pseudo Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules are introduced and equivalently related to (semi-)C*-Fredholm properties of their synthesis operators. The notion of the excess of a C*-module frame is introduced, taking values in related C* algebras. Indicators for possible erasures of frame elements are described with the aim to preserve robustness of frames. Introducing a new notion of pseudo-Riesz-Weyl sequences in the standard Hilbert C*-module $l_2(A)$ we reverse the found correspondence by assuming the associated synthesis operator of a Bessel sequence to be (upper semi-)C*-Weyl. Furthermore, we deduce from the invariance of (upper semi-)C*-Fredholm and C*-Riesz-Weyl properties of synthesis operators with respect to ''compact'' perturbations the perturbation invariance of the respective classes of module Bessel sequences.
papers.title: Near-Riesz and pseudo-Riesz bases of Hilbert C*-modules and semi-C*-Fredholm operators

papers.abstract: In this paper, the dynamical system analysis has been performed to analyze the dynamical behavior of the Universe in $f(R,L_m,T)$ gravity with a scalar field. A well motivated potential function and the linear form of the functional $f(R,L_m,T)$ have been incorporated into the Friedmann equation, and the autonomous dynamical system has been framed by introducing dimensionless variables. The stability behavior of the critical points is obtained and analyzed based on their corresponding eigenvalues. Moreover, cosmological parameters such as the deceleration parameter and the dynamical parameters such as equation of state and density parameters are obtained using the dimensionless variables. It has been observed that the system provides critical points that describe different evolutionary phases of the Universe.
papers.title: Evolutionary Phase of Universe in $f(R,L_m,T)$ Gravity: The Dynamical System Analysis

papers.abstract: Soliton-based computing architectures have recently emerged as a promising avenue to overcome fundamental limitations of conventional information technologies, the von Neumann bottleneck. In this context, magnetic skyrmions have been widely considered for in-situ processing devices due to their mobility and enhanced lifetime in materials with broken inversion symmetry. However, modern applications in non-volatile reservoir or neuromorphic computing raise the additional demand for non-linear inter-soliton interactions. Here, we report that solitons in easy-plane magnets, such as bimerons and antibimerons, show greater versatility and potential for non-linear interactions than skyrmions and antiskyrmions, making them superior candidates for this class of applications. Using first-principles and transition state theory, we predict the coexistence of degenerate bimerons and antibimerons at zero field in a van der Waals heterostructure Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$/Cr$_2$Ge$_2$Te$_6$ -- an experimentally feasible system. We demonstrate that, owing to their distinct structural symmetry, bimerons exhibit fundamentally different behavior from skyrmions and cannot be regarded as their in-plane counterparts, as is often assumed. This distinction leads to unique properties of bimerons and antibimerons, which arise from the unbroken rotational symmetry in easy-plane magnets. These range from anisotropic soliton-soliton interactions to strong entropic effects on their lifetime, driven by the non-local nature of thermal excitations. Our findings reveal a broader richness of solitons in easy-plane magnets and underline their unique potential for spintronic devices.
papers.title: Lifetime of bimerons and antibimerons in two-dimensional magnets

papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, technological advances have assisted individuals to gain access to legal information, enhance the efficiency of legal services, and streamline dispute resolution. More recently, the proliferation of generative artificial intelligence has reinforced this emphasis on firm-level productivity, with commercial legal practice increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence tools to automate document creation and optimise case management. While commercial technology focuses on productivity, community organisations are exploring how artificial intelligence can level the playing field for marginalised communities. Far less attention has been given to free, direct-to-consumer legal technologies, as these models are often unprofitable. Consequently, justice technology scholarship has overlooked a distinct class of technology: digital reporting platforms that enable people to record their experiences of harm, while simultaneously aggregating those accounts into a body of evidence capable of supporting advocacy, institutional accountability, and law reform. Crucially, experiences of discrimination and administrative abuse are often dismissed by oversight bodies as individual grievances. To understand the transformative potential of these platforms, this article asks two questions. First, how can digital reporting close the knowledge and power gap for marginalised communities interacting with the legal system? Second, how can these tools collect evidence to hold institutions accountable, drive change and contribute to a more just society?
papers.title: The Moving Frontier: How the National Justice Project Is Using Digital Technology to Expand Access to Justice

papers.abstract: On July 23, 2026, at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, the International Mathematical Union announced the award of the Gauss Prize to Yurii Evgenievich Nesterov -- an award for mathematical work with significant applications outside mathematics. This article explains the mathematical content of the recognized work of Yu. E. Nesterov and traces its influence on modern computational practice. The exposition is based on a concept that Yu. E. Nesterov himself regards as one of his main results: the classical complexity theory of convex optimization is oriented toward a black-box oracle, but its pessimistic bounds can be overcome by using a priori information about the internal structure of the objective function. We trace Yu. E. Nesterov's scientific career, then introduce the language of oracle complexity together with a classification of objective function models (geometric, algebraic, and structural), and subsequently discuss his main results in chronological order: the fast gradient method, fast automatic differentiation, the theory of self-concordant barriers and polynomial-time interior-point methods, the $π/2$ theorem, the stable dynamics model of traffic flows, the smoothing technique, primal-dual methods, cubic regularization of Newton's method, the modified Gauss--Newton scheme, coordinate descent methods and methods for huge-scale problems, gradient-free methods, universal gradient methods, implementable tensor methods, and "superfast" methods. Each topic is accompanied by historical background, precise statements specifying the problem class, oracle, and type of guarantee, examples, and a discussion of the current state of the art.
papers.title: How to Look Inside the Black Box: A Survey of Yu. E. Nesterov's Contributions (On the Award of the 2026 Gauss Prize)

papers.abstract: This Ph.D. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. In Chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in Hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. The next chapters are then devoted to my publications. In the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time Type II blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-ν$, where $ν> 1$ in 4D and $ν> 3$ in 5D. The major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. In 4D, we essentially follow the Krieger-Schlag-Tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. By contrast, the 5D case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms. In Chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical Lp and Schauder estimates for parabolic equations. Then, in Chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. Under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. The method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. We also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. Finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by Struwe and Qing using energy arguments and the Palais-Smale condition.
papers.title: On blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow

papers.abstract: Designing materials for thermal management requires knowing where heat flows, not only how much. Within harmonic (Allen$--$Feldman) theory we develop two local descriptions and test them on amorphous silicon. The first, a projection of the conductivity $κ$ onto atoms, depends on how the potential energy is divided among atoms (a "gauge"); we find the dependence moderate, 23% of the map's spatial standard deviation at single sites and 9.5% over regions of radius 0.4 nm, apart from a uniform offset of 0.8% of $κ$. The second avoids the division altogether. It is the exact response of $κ$ to the mass of each atom and the stiffness of each bond, it obeys an Euler sum rule, and it contains the heat-flow map as one of three exact terms. In amorphous and paracrystalline silicon, with ACE, GAP-18 and Keating force constants, the two maps are anti-correlated: where little heat flows a heavier atom lowers $κ$, and where much heat flows it tends to raise it. The explanation is local softness. The harmonic vibrational amplitude of each atom predicts both maps, and at room temperature the anti-correlation largely disappears at fixed amplitude, in a 32,768-atom replica as well; below about 100 K a component remains that softness does not capture. Thus soft regions, which carry little heat, act through the mixing of vibrational modes about 1$--$2 meV apart. In paracrystalline silicon the grains conduct more heat per atom, while the disordered matrix controls the response. Exact recalculations show that the response map guides the placement of dispersed substituents and locates the region that limits transport across an amorphous/crystalline interface.
papers.title: Where heat flows and where to change it: gauge-free sensitivity maps of thermal conductivity in disordered solids

papers.abstract: We prove that the integrality gap of the Călinescu-Karloff-Rabani relaxation for Minimum Multiway Cut is at least $1.2325$ when the number of terminals is large. By a result of Manokaran, Naor, Raghavendra, and Schwartz (2008), it is therefore NP-hard, under the Unique Games Conjecture, to approximate Minimum Multiway Cut within a factor of $1.2325$. This improves the previously best known lower bound of $1.20016$ due to Bérczi, Chandrasekaran, Király, and Madan (2020).
papers.title: An Integrality-Gap Lower Bound of 1.2325 for Minimum Multiway Cut

papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce Octopus, a single-model multi-agent RL framework in which all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph (DAG) of KV states through five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit). Octopus combines three co-designed mechanisms: (1) Zero-Copy Radix Forking, which spawns branches as $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cursor views over shared physical KV pages; (2) Attention-Only KV Mounting, which mounts a sibling thread's terminal KV blocks directly into full-attention layers while bypassing linear-recurrent states (Gated DeltaNet / Mamba-2), cutting off-task hijacking by $21\times$ ($57.9\% \to 2.7\%$) while retaining $92.2\%$ of full-text mutual information at zero extra KV allocation; and (3) a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer, which packs all episode branches into one block-sparse attention pass and assigns counterfactual branch credit via leave-one-branch-out marginal rewards. Trained end-to-end with GRPO on Qwen3.5-4B over a sparse BM25 corpus, Octopus reaches $49.6\%$ accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus ($+17.5$ points over single-agent GRPO at 143K context and $+12.5$ points over text-summary multi-agent RL) and $51.2\%$ on OpenResearcher, outperforming dense-retrieval agents up to $250\times$ larger while increasing training throughput $3.3\times$ and cutting peak KV memory $2.8\times$.
